#2148. Arsenal vs Hull City preview: Gunners face draw specialists at the Emirates

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal have the opportunity to strengthen their position in the Premier League table when they welcome Hull City to the Emirates Stadium on Saturday.

Mikel Arteta’s side secured a three-point lead after their 1-0 victory over Liverpool at Anfield and then followed it up with a 2-1 win in the Champions League against Slavia Prague on Wednesday.

The Gunners have won four games in a row but are looking to stretch their lead to six points ahead of Manchester City’s clash against Nottingham Forest later on Saturday. They are undefeated at home this season.

However, Hull will be looking to cause problems in North London.

Sergej Jakirovic’s side sit 11th after collecting 11 points from their opening nine league matches.

They have drawn five times, sharing the highest number of stalemates in the division. Three of their last four league fixtures have also ended level.

They drew 2-2 with Ipswich Town in their last game, but they needed to get back on track after falling behind. Recently they have failed to convert good performances into wins.

Despite Arsenal expecting to dominate possession, Hull’s 5-man defence may cause them problems.

The visitors have also had defensive issues recently, as they have failed to keep a clean sheet in their last seven games in all competitions. This may lead to chances being created for the Gunners attackers.

Arteta has to deal with his squad after the midweek trip to Prague. William Saliba is back in contention after recovering from his back injury but Cristhian Mosquera may stay in the squad if he is not rushed back in.

Ezri Konsa is a doubt after being withdrawn from Wednesday’s game with a knee problem. Bukayo Saka is also still sidelined as is Max Dowman.

Hull will be missing Matt Crooks who is suspended. Eliot Matazo, Matt Targett, Darko Gyabi, Ilyas Ansah and Charlie Hughes are also expected to miss out.

Raya; Timber, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori; Guimarães, Rice; Madueke, Ødegaard, Tzolis; Havertz.

Tzolakis; Coyle, Ajayi, Egan, Mendy, Giles; Belloumi, Iroegbunam, Slater, Stroud; McBurnie.

Arsenal will face Hull City at the Emirates Stadium on Saturday, November 7. Kick off is at 3pm GMT.

Despite the fact that Hull has a tendency to draw, Arsenal remains a strong favorite to win this match. Arteta’s team will want to earn as many points as possible ahead of the international break.

#2147. Thomas Tuchel makes Noni Madueke decision as five Arsenal stars earn England call-ups

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Noni Madueke has missed another England opportunity, despite making an encouraging impression during his recent run in the Arsenal starting line-up.

Thomas Tuchel has named his 25-man squad for the Nations League fixtures against Croatia and Spain in November, but Arsenal winger Madueke misses out again after failing to make the cut following a missed international camp.

He has been left out despite making the most of Bukayo Saka’s absence to increase his involvement under Mikel Arteta.

Madueke scored in the recent Premier League win against Nottingham Forest and then again in Wednesday’s Champions League win against Slavia Prague.

He had a legitimate claim to be named in the squad, and Tuchel admitted that Madueke was very close to being included.

The England boss acknowledged that Madueke has benefitted from his extra games at Arsenal due to Saka’s injury.

But Tuchel chose to keep the same front three that he had during the last international camp. The German wants to reward those players who have earned their place in the team and not make changes every time they are playing well at club level.

This means Madueke will be left frustrated, having to wait until next time.

Madueke has played under Tuchel before, so it shows how much he thinks of him as a player. He featured in England’s 2026 World Cup campaign, so it is noticeable that he was left out this time.

Although he can’t control the battle for places, he will now be able to continue building his case. With Saka still injured, he will have the chance to play more regularly and solidify his place in Arteta’s plans.

However, Madueke is not the only player at Arsenal who has had positive news.

Declan Rice, Eberechi Eze, Ezri Konsa and Myles Lewis-Skelly have all earned or retained their spots in Tuchel’s squad. Ben White also comes back into the England squad, having missed the last camp.

It is another chance for White to re-establish himself on the world stage after his knee injury kept him out of the World Cup.

It also means Arsenal have five players in the squad after Saka was left out due to injury.

England play Croatia at Wembley on November 12 before heading to Spain on November 15. Madueke will be watching from home, knowing he was almost part of the squad.

Now he needs to build on his recent form and become a consistent performer for Arsenal. Whilst Tuchel has left the door open, Madueke needs to give the England boss another reason to change his mind.

#2145. Arsenal transfer interest faces major obstacle as Santos secure £83m teenage talent

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal may have to rethink their interest in Santos forward Ignacio Pereira after the Brazilian club secured the teenager’s future with a substantial release clause.

The 16-year-old has caught the eye of a number of European clubs after an impressive campaign in Santos’ youth teams. The likes of Arsenal are said to have been watching his progress.

However, Santos have acted swiftly to secure the services of one of their most exciting young talents. Pereira signed his first professional contract with the club on November 4, tying him to the club until December 2029.

The deal also includes a 100 million euro release clause (around £83.4 million), according to Brazilian journalist Bruno Lima from UOL.

This poses a major problem for Arsenal if they are looking to sign the Argentine but also offers a lot of security for Santos, as they want to develop him as a first-team player.

Pereira has signed a new deal amid increasing interest in his development. Reports in Brazil have previously said that Arsenal, Real Betis, AC Milan, Lille, Standard Liège and Zenit are all keeping an eye on the rising star.

The club have now secured his services for another three years. The new agreement was awaiting registration with the Brazilian Football Confederation when the details emerged.

Pereira has spent three years at Santos, having joined from Juventude in 2023. He previously developed at Grêmio before moving to the São Paulo club.

Pereira has certainly lived up to the expectations. He scored an impressive 6 goals in 17 games in the Brazilian Under-17 Championship, making him the second-highest scorer for Santos. He also scored 4 goals in the Paulista Under-17 Championship.

This is very promising. It is his first season playing at under-17 level.

Pereira has been compared to Julián Álvarez due to his mobility and ability to play outside the box.

But the youngster cites another big name up front as his main inspiration. According to UOL, he cites Manchester City’s Erling Haaland as his inspiration, while Lionel Messi is still his football idol.

His profile suggests a versatile number nine who can play lower down the pitch, be an attacking midfielder and play with another striker. He has impressed the youth coaches at Santos with his finishing ability, physicality and desire to win.

He has a long way to go. Reports from Brazil suggest that Santos want to improve his tactical awareness and behaviour before making him more responsible.

He is being considered by the club for inclusion in their squad for the 2027 Copa São Paulo de Futebol Júnior (known as Copinha) and could start on the bench.

This interest from Arsenal does not necessarily mean that there is an imminent move for Pereira. The player is only 16, and a potential deal is made much more complicated due to a new contract.

Maybe the best course of action for Mikel Arteta’s recruitment team is to keep an eye on him. Santos has made it clear where they stand, and Pereira can now work towards his dream. Being in their first team.

#2143. Arsenal handed William Saliba boost as Arteta considers defender’s return

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

The William Saliba Arsenal boost comes at a crucial time. Saliba can use the November international break to build up his fitness after missing out on France’s latest squad.

Arteta confirmed that the defender had returned to full training ahead of Arsenal’s Champions League meeting with Slavia Prague. He also completed 45 minutes in a behind-closed-doors-friendly last week as he stepped up his recovery.

However, Saliba did not feature in the 2-1 victory. Arteta included him in the matchday squad for the first time this season, but the Frenchman remained an unused substitute.

It means he was not selected by Zinedine Zidane for France’s Nations League games against Italy and Turkey. This gives Arsenal a chance to continue working on his recovery. He will not be travelling for international games or playing in competitive matches.

Saliba has not featured since he suffered a back injury during France’s World Cup semi-final against Spain in July. Arteta has had to find alternatives in central defence in the early stages of the campaign.

Since transferring to Arsenal from Aston Villa in August, Konsa has played a part in filling the gap left by Saliba. His presence in the centre of defence complements Gabriel Magalhães and gives Arteta more options.

The England defender is also expected to be fit for the match against Hull City on Saturday. According to Arteta, the player’s replacement in the game against Slavia Prague was just a precaution after he reported some discomfort.

The fact that he has made a recovery means that Arsenal have the option to control how Saliba returns. Arteta has the possibility of bringing Saliba back gradually, as Konsa is ready to play and Mosquera is also available.

But Saliba’s return still matters. He needs to get back in shape before the fixtures start getting tougher after the international break.

Arteta has made it clear he will respect whatever decision Zidane makes regarding Saliba’s availability but acknowledges that he needs some game time after being out for so long.

France will play Italy on November 12 and then Turkey three days later. This means Saliba will be missing those matches, as Zidane named his 23-man squad on Friday.

This means he will be able to continue to be monitored by the club at their London Colney training ground. He won’t be able to return to play in international games ahead of his first appearance for the club.

Arsenal will be hoping that he can use the extra time to get himself ready for the next set of games, including a trip to Newcastle before playing Borussia Dortmund and Manchester City at home.

Arteta will be keen to have Saliba back in contention but will be focused on getting him back at the right time.

There is some immediate optimism on Konsa’s fitness for the game against Hull. But more importantly, Saliba has now progressed to a point where he can be included in the planning process.

#2142. Dundee United 1-1 Motherwell: Backheel beauty earns hosts a point

Dundee United and Motherwell had to be content with a share of the spoils in a 1-1 draw after an entertaining Premiership contest at Tannadice.

Steelmen skipper Lukas Fadinger gave his side the lead from the penalty spot, with Jesse Randall equalising for the home side before the break with a moment of magic.

Neither side could find a winner in the second half but United have now extended their unbeaten run to seven games to remain sixth in the table while Motherwell stay ninth.

The Steelmen took the lead in the ninth minute. Tawanda Maswanhise tumbled in the home box under a challenge from Dylan Tait but the linesman’s flag went up for offside.

However, referee Ryan Lee was called over to the pitchside monitor by the VAR Andrew Dallas and decided to award a penalty. Fadinger stepped up and sent United goalkeeper Jack Walton the wrong way.

Shortly after, United were claiming for a penalty of their own when Zac Sapsford went down in a challenge with Emmanuel Longelo but the whistler flashed a yellow card at the Terrors striker for diving.

Maswanhise then created an opening of his own, embarking on a barnstorming run but his shot flew straight to Walton, who easily gathered.

Motherwell’s Ibrahim Said was next to try his luck from 22 yards but again his effort was straight at Walton and then Sapsford hit a snap-shot that was well saved by the visitors’ goalie Alexander Paulsen.

Walton was called into action again in the 28th minute when Tom Sparrow found Longelo inside the United box with the defender hitting a shot into the ground that the keeper had to acrobatically tip over, before Daniel Bennie went close at the other end with a header.

Paulsen then made two smart saves in quick succession from shots by Lyall Cameron and then Tait.

However, the keeper could not prevent United equalising in the 41st minute when the ball found its way to Randall inside the Motherwell box and with his back to the goal, the New Zealander produced a cheeky backheel that flew past Paulsen.

Randall had another chance at the start of the second half but this time his composure deserted him and he blasted well over the bar.

Longelo then found himself in a promising position but his curling shot was deflected for a corner.

The hosts hit back with Bennie cutting in from the left before striking a fierce shot that was well blocked by Motherwell defender Martin Moorman.

There was a big scare for the hosts in the 62nd minute when Bert Esselink was robbed of possession by Seb Palmer-Houlden but the striker’s shot flew just over.

It was United’s turn to threaten next with Michael Forbes producing a powerful header that was cleared off the line by Moorman.

The hosts had a great chance to snatch a winner in the 87th minute but Josh Rawlins completely fluffed his lines just two yards with Randall then coming close with a shot.

#2141. “We should have reacted better” | Frank admission won’t bring the points back | West Ham News

Down in ninth place, outside even the play-off places, is hardly where West Ham, the pre-season favourites and the ‘big hitters descended into the Championship’ expected to find themselves after fifteen games. This, the most competitive of leagues, throws up unexpected results each and every week and West Ham have, simply, not been up to speed.

The week after week excuses of Nuno Espírito Santo have been replaced by the emotional, heart-on-his-sleeve reassurances of an albeit shell- shocked Scott Parker, but it is clear there’s a huge challenge ahead.

Scott Parker may have a more engaging style than Nuno but excuses only count for so long

Talk is cheap, there are only so many times we as fans we can be told that the team should have tried harder, prepared better, worked more, et cetera, et cetera, et cetera..before our eyes glaze over and disappointment gives way to anger – as was displayed at full time yesterday.

Defender Dinos Mavropanos, to his credit, takes his fair share of the blame himself for the defensive lapse that led to Blackburn’s second goal when he and his team mates switched off, anticipating a stoppage for Max Kilman’s head injury instead of playing to the whistle:

“I mean, yes, it’s tough, this league with no VAR coming around, it’s difficult to speak about these situations,” he explained

“I’m not going to blame the referee because at the end it’s a decision I can’t change. But again, I think we should have reacted better and not concede this kind of goal.” (whufc.com)

Exactly so, Dinos. However frank acceptances like this don’t bring the points back. Forget automatic promotion. Eleven points dropped in the last four games is relegation form, whichever way you look at it.

West Ham pay for the lack of competition for centre back places, as we’ve already pointed out repeatedly. Taking the blame for mistakes is one thing. Not repeating them is a whole other set of problems.

I still watch YouTube repeats of the Cup Final of 2006 hoping in vain that Shaka Hislop grows another six inches and stops Steven Gerrard's injury time equaliser. Can tell I'm getting old knowing I watched both Mark Noble's debut and his last game at West Ham. #2140. An open letter to Newcastle United fans

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

An open letter to my fellow Newcastle United fans – The 12th man.

‘We call ourselves the best supporters in the world. We wear our black and white stripes with pride. We sing about loyalty, passion, history and what it means to be a Geordie. We talk about St James’ Park being a fortress, about the noise, the atmosphere and the incredible connection between this club and its supporters.

Are we actually living up to the names we give ourselves?

Because, if I’m being honest, what we’ve witnessed at St James’ Park, particularly towards the back end of last season and continuing into this new chapter, has been difficult to watch. Not because of the football alone, but because of the attitude coming from the stands.

The atmosphere has, at times, become toxic. The groans, the negativity, the frustration, the booing at half-time and full-time. Players being written off before they’ve had a proper opportunity to settle. A new team being judged against the standards of a team that took years to build.

And I can’t help thinking that as Newcastle United fans we’ve lost sight of something incredibly important.

Look at what has happened at this football club. We’ve experienced significant change. A new manager, the loss of our club captain, the departure of experienced senior players and leaders, both on and off the pitch. The familiar faces, personalities and voices that helped shape the identity of this team have changed.

The dressing room has changed. The leadership has changed. The dynamics have changed. The team is evolving.

And yet, almost before this new group has had the opportunity to find its feet, we’ve been quick to turn on them.

Did we think a new manager would walk through the door, inherit a changing squad and everything would immediately click into place? That new partnerships, understanding, confidence and leadership would magically appear overnight?

Players need time to understand each other. New leaders need time to emerge. A manager needs time to implement his ideas. Confidence needs nurturing, not destroying.

And that last point is particularly important.

Imagine being a player walking out at St James’ Park, knowing that one misplaced pass, one poor decision or one disappointing half could be met with a chorus of groans or boos.

Imagine trying to build confidence in an unfamiliar team when the very people who are supposed to lift you are making you feel ten feet tall one minute and ten feet under the next.

We all want to win. We all want to see Newcastle competing at the highest level. Nobody is suggesting we should accept poor performances, abandon ambition or pretend everything is perfect when it isn’t.

We’re football supporters. We have every right to be frustrated, disappointed and demanding.

But there is a difference between demanding better and actively contributing to making things worse.

There is a difference between supporting a football club and only supporting it when things are going well.

This is Newcastle United. We know our history. We’ve experienced the highs, the lows, the heartbreak and the near misses. We’ve stood on the terraces through some truly difficult times. We know what loyalty means.

So why, now that the club is trying to build something, are we so quick to turn on the very people representing it?

The irony is that we constantly talk about the incredible atmosphere at St James’ Park. Opposition supporters talk about it. Players talk about it. Managers talk about it. It’s one of the things that makes Newcastle United special.

But that atmosphere isn’t created by the architecture, the pitch or the players alone.

We are the 12th man. Not a marketing slogan. Not something we sing about when we’re winning. Not something we switch on for the big European nights and switch off when a game isn’t going our way.

When the team is struggling, that’s when they need us most. When confidence is low, that’s when the noise should be loudest. When a new player makes a mistake, that’s when we should be getting behind him, not making him dread his next touch.

Imagine what it could do for a young player, a new signing or someone finding their feet in a different role to hear 52,000 people behind them rather than against them.

Imagine the confidence that could give a team still learning to play together.

We pride ourselves on being different. On being passionate, fiercely loyal and united behind our club. Well, perhaps it’s time we started showing it again.

Let’s stop comparing every new player with someone who has left. Let’s stop expecting a team in transition to perform like a settled side. Let’s give the manager and his players the opportunity to build relationships, develop an identity and find their rhythm.

And, above all, let’s remember that supporting Newcastle United isn’t conditional on the scoreline.

There will be poor performances. There will be mistakes. There will be frustrating afternoons, and Monday night catastrophes. There will be games when we leave St James’ Park wondering what on earth we’ve just watched.

But we should never allow frustration to become the defining feature of our support.

We have an opportunity here. A new chapter, a new group of players and a chance to build something together. The club has changed, and perhaps it’s time we changed our approach too.

The players have a responsibility to give everything for that shirt. The manager has a responsibility to get the best out of his squad. The board has a responsibility to take the club forward.

And we, the supporters, have a responsibility too.

Our job is to make St James’ Park a place opposition teams fear and our own players feel inspired.

So the next time we go through the turnstiles, let’s think about what we’re bringing into that stadium.

Let’s sing a little louder. Let’s get behind the players. Let’s lift them when they’re struggling. Let’s make some noise when things aren’t going our way.

Let’s be the supporters we constantly tell the rest of the world we are.

Because being the best fans in the world isn’t something you earn when your team wins.

It’s something you prove when they need you most.

We are Newcastle United. We are the Toon Army. We are the 12th man.

It’s about time we started acting like it.’

#2139. Arsenal transfer news: Arsenal set January transfer priorities as Fabrizio Romano delivers Piero Hincapié update

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

In Arsenal transfer news, Arsenal could approach the January transfer window with a different focus after Fabrizio Romano revealed that Mikel Arteta has no intention of weakening his defensive options.

Piero Hincapié has been linked with a move to Barcelona. There have been reports that a deal could be done involving Alejandro Balde, but Romano expects the Ecuadorian to stay at Emirates Stadium.

Arsenal have been strengthening their defensive department under Arteta. Hincapié only made the switch permanently from Bayer Leverkusen in the summer after joining on loan.

Despite competition, the 24-year-old is a key player in Arteta’s plans. His versatility to play in either a centre back or left back role gives Arteta a valuable option.

However, we can also gain insight into where Arsenal should target their recruitment from Romano’s latest comments. Instead of changing their defensive options, it could be an opportunity to improve their attacking options.

Despite competition, the 24-year-old is a key player in Arteta’s plans. His versatility to play in either a centre back or left back role gives Arteta a valuable option.

However, we can also gain insight into where Arsenal should target their recruitment from Romano’s latest comments. Instead of changing their defensive options, it could be an opportunity to improve their attacking options.

However, Arsenal have little incentive to let him leave halfway through the season, as losing a two-in-one defender will cause problems for Arteta, given how much they need to do in multiple competitions.

Romano’s comments suggest that Arsenal are happy with their existing defensive unit and don’t want to cause any disruption to their balance. He also suggested that Hincapié is an important player for them, meaning he’s unlikely to leave in January.

That leaves Barcelona needing to explore alternative targets if they want to strengthen their backline. A deal involving Balde and Hincapié does not currently appear to be a realistic option.

The more interesting part of Romano’s report is Arsenal’s potential business at the other end of the field.

He feels they will be looking to make a move if the right attacking player comes up for grabs. But he doesn’t think they will make a signing just because they can in January.

This highlights the issues clubs face with mid-season transfers. Often selling clubs will be unwilling to lose key players, and finding suitable replacements can be tough.

As such, Arsenal are likely to look at the market to see what they can do. However, it looks like there could still be a forward brought in.

This is an important distinction. The point being made here is that whilst there is speculation around one particular player, Romano has indicated that Arsenal can strengthen their attacking options. This is not to say that any particular move is happening.

If Arteta keeps Hincapié, then Arsenal will maintain their defensive stability and possibly gain another option in attack.

Over the next few weeks we will get a better understanding of what is available to them. But for now it looks like Arsenal are not keen to lose Hincapié but will look to strengthen their attacking options if the right deal comes along.

#2137. Arsenal vs Hull City preview: Arteta sticks with winning formula as Gunners target another three points

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal have resisted the temptation to rotate after their victory at Anfield, with Mikel Arteta naming the same starting XI for Saturday’s meeting with Hull City.

Arsenal welcome Championship side Hull City to the Emirates Stadium, looking to strengthen their grip on the top spot after collecting 24 points from their opening nine Premier League games. However, their tally of just 14 goals suggests Arteta’s side still have work to do in the final third.

Arteta has again chosen to partner Ezri Konsa and Gabriel Magalhães in defence. William Saliba was left out despite pre-match talk that he would be named in the starting XI. Bukayo Saka and Max Dowman are also missing from the squad.

Noni Madueke will carry the right. Tzolis starts on the opposite flank. Kai Havertz will lead the line. Viktor Gyökeres, Eberechi Eze and Mikel Merino add attacking options from the bench.

Arsenal predicted starting XI: Raya; Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Guimarães, Rice, Ødegaard; Madueke, Havertz, Tzolis.

Substitutes: Arrizabalaga, White, Mosquera, Hincapié, Lewis-Skelly, Zubimendi, Merino, Eze, Gyökeres.

Hull are coming into this game ranked 11th in the league after five draws in their first nine games. They’ve not won in their last eight games but can cause problems for any opposition.

They look like playing a defensive game with Slater, Iroegbunam and Gourna-Douath in the midfield to protect the backline. McBurnie and Cho will give them some attacking options.

Hull starting XI: Tzolakis; Coyle, Ajayi, Egan, Mendy, Stroud; Slater, Iroegbunam, Gourna-Douath; McBurnie, Cho.

Substitutes: Butland, Giles, Thomas, Gelhardt, Hjerto-Dahl, Norton-Cuffy, Herrington, Mouzakitis, Vaz.

McBurnie is just one booking away from suspension for the clash against Brighton on November 22 but may make an important impact in the physical battle with Gabriel.

Hull have not scored at the Emirates since 2014 but will look to turn that around. However, their main concern will be to ensure they keep Arsenal quiet for as long as possible.

Arsenal will need to find ways to break down the likely tight Hull backline.

Ødegaard and Rice will be key in keeping possession and creating chances, whilst Madueke and Tzolis will create width and movement.

Hull may be exposed to threat in case they are trapped in defence for too long, but Arteta can use Gyökeres if Havertz is having difficulties doing anything productive.

A win for Arsenal will give them a six-point lead. Manchester City will be looking to get all three points when they face Nottingham Forest later on Saturday.

The visitors will look to create an uncomfortable afternoon for the Gunners.

Arsenal have enough quality to take all three points, but Hull will not make it easy for them. I expect this to be a tight game, and the Gunners will win by a small margin.

#2136. Scott Parker’s bold gamble which went virtually unnoticed in Ewood Park defeat | West Ham News

The headlines don’t make for good reading at the moment for West Ham United fans. Whether it be the Sun or the NY Times, the big hitters are queueing up to put the boot in with tales of fan unrest and not fit to wear the shirt chanting which makes for good copy but does nothing for morale, on or off the pitch.

In fact, if we’re being honest, it is when his employment should have started rather than in the mist of a Cardiff City November midweek fixture that he’d not had a moment to prepare for. 20/20 hindsight maybe, but the firing of Nuno could have been timed better.

Mayers could solve West Ham’s left back problems – if only the other issues were so easily fixed

Anyways there’s one change which Parker’s team – or the manager himself, who knows – has already made to this West Ham team that does bode well for the future, despite the negativity around the club right now.

Dropping the stand-in left back Morato and elevating youngster Ezra Mayers to the starting eleven was a bold gamble which could have gone horribly wrong.

Mayers, remember, appeared after the dreadful first 45 minutes midweek, and was described as making “an impressive impact”(the72.co.uk) in the second half against Cardiff.  At Ewood Park he took to the position with the relish of one who has been waiting a long time for his chance.

Unlike his academy contemporary Olle Scarles, Mayers is both pacy and far more comfortable wizzing down the wing into an overlap – which he did frequently outside his winger Edvin Austbø – as well as carrying out his defensive duties with decent aplomb considering his was the losing side.

The Hammers may have problems galore but I’d suggest the left back issue is one which Parker’s gamble has sorted. Logically it might also free up Morato to bolster the centre back options – with Kilman suspended, perhaps we’ll get to see the Brazilian doing the job he’s actually here for. What’s the worst that can happen?

From the old Bobby Moore Upper to the Billy Bonds' stand these days - I've been watching since '03 and a supporter since about 1970.. Favourite player - Dean Ashton: Curse you Shaun Wright-Phillips. I still watch YouTube repeats of the Cup Final of 2006 hoping in vain that Shaka Hislop grows another six inches and stops Steven Gerrard's injury time equaliser. Can tell I'm getting old knowing I watched both Mark Noble's debut and his last game at West Ham. Pulling on a Claret and Blue replica shirt still makes me feel the same butterflies as when I was seven years old. Magic.

Mayers also hit in a fantastic low cross, just begging to be knocked into the back of the net.

As you say might be first chance to see Morato at left-CB as he is left-footed. RB + Dinos/Golambeckis, Morato, Mayers against Preston in a back 4, even a back 3 in the 2nd half if chasing a game – but that’s a bit adventurous and what do I know? One step at a time perhaps.

If Morato & Mayers can combine well, get to trust each other that would help. Mayers & Austbo already seems to be effective down the left and we also have Ajala who can play on the left side and knows Mayers well.

Mayers shows some reliability too. He played left-CB (left-footed) for U21s so he is used to shouldering responsibility at the heart of a defense which stands him in good stead. He seems like the type of player who can step up and develop through this season to become a reliable and accomplished starter for next season in whichever league we are in; he seems to have all the qualities and he is raring to go.

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal needed a moment of quality from their captain to overcome Hull City and claim a narrow 1-0 Premier League victory at the Emirates Stadium.

Martin Ødegaard scored in the 72nd minute as the hosts struggled to break down a resolute Hull side. It was much like I expected in my match preview, as Arsenal had to work hard to win this game.

The result gives them an extended lead at the top of the table. Ahead of Manchester City’s clash with Nottingham Forest. However, Mikel Arteta will be aware that his team did not play well in this game. It was far from a walk in the park.

Hull arrived at London looking to play an attacking game. Jakirovic’s side were well organised and looked to launch quick counter attacks.

They did have some positive moments in the first half, but Arsenal struggled to get into their attacking rhythm. Kai Havertz couldn’t capitalise on one good chance created by Ødegaard.

The hosts were hopeful of taking the lead after Havertz fell to the ground in the box after being pulled back by Nobel Mendy.

However, referee Farai Hallam’s initial decision was overturned after a VAR review showed Havertz was offside earlier in the attack, so Arsenal’s penalty was cancelled.

Another frustrating moment for the home side, who failed to score during the first half, despite dominating possession.

Arsenal came out strong after the break. However, Hull were still causing problems. Lewie Coyle was also walking a fine line after a yellow card in the first half and a late challenge on Christos Tzolis.

Arteta made a three-man change on the hour mark, bringing on Viktor Gyökeres and Mikel Merino for Havertz and Declan Rice. Six minutes later he brought on Eberechi Eze and Piero Hincapié.

The breakthrough came from Madueke, forcing Konstantinos Tzolakis into action. The Hull keeper couldn’t hold his shot, and Ødegaard was quickest to react, scoring from the rebound.

The captain’s strike took the frustration out of Arsenal’s efforts and was a reward for their perseverance. It also provided another vital moment for the Norwegian. He’s had a tough campaign so far due to injuries.

Despite going behind, Hull never gave up in their search for an equaliser. However, Arsenal held on to their lead.

Arsenal dominated the game with 67% of possession and 21 shots, compared to just seven for Hull. Tzolakis put in a number of key interventions to keep the scoreline respectable.

Although they weren’t at their best, Arsenal were able to perform in the key moments of the game. Ødegaard’s goal meant that the Gunners earned three points and are sitting top of the Premier League heading into the international break.

#2133. Lies, damn lies, and statistics (and Newcastle United…)

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

As a Newcastle United fan I was pondering that famous saying, “There are lies, damned lies and statistics”, which is used to describe the persuasive power of statistics to bolster weak arguments.

Here’s an argument that uses statistics for you to consider, the merits of which probably depend on whether you want to give Matthias Jaissle the benefit of the doubt or not.

It should, because not only is that Newcastle United’s Premier League record after the opening ten games of this campaign, it is the same record that we had this time last year after ten games.

Okay, the goal difference this time at minus three is slightly worse – it was only minus one at the same point in 2025/26, but look deeper and when you consider the teams we’ve faced in those opening ten games, we are a staggering five points better off compared to last season in the corresponding fixtures.

In our opening fixture, we drew with Liverpool (should have won, but never mind) whilst the previous season, that lot won at SJP (they shouldn’t have done, but that’s also irrelevant).

Bournemouth at home and Fulham; defeats last time out in those fixtures. This season two points gained.

That away win at Selhurst Park gave us three more points than in the previous campaign and in all our other matches, barring Leeds away, we’ve acquired the same number of points as last season; that defeat at Elland Road being the only game this season where we have recorded a worse outcome, one less point than last season away at Leeds.

I think so. I think Matthias Jaissle isn’t doing so bad.

Of course, we want to do better than we are, but it’s early days, and I think yesterday’s improved performance at Craven Cottage gives us a modicum of reasons to be optimistic.

Note: the relegated teams have been swapped out with promoted teams in the positions they finished in last season so for third bottom West Ham, read Coventry City (who won the Championship). Similarly bottom club Wolves have been replaced by play-off winners Hull City.

#2132. Nils Koppen deserves credit as West Ham ‘dodged huge summer transfer bullet’

There is a tendency to lump every player together in a failing team and declare them all unfit for purpose, as the West Ham fans’ much publicised chanting at Ewood Park might suggest. However, the boiling over of a couple of years of frustration and anger, aimed at the current occupants of the claret and blue shirts, need not be taken as voicing disapproval of the whole squad.

In fact, there are some positive signs – Ezra Mayers, as we wrote elsewhere this morning- gives us all cause for optimism.

I’d wager that another starter against Blackburn, Edvin Austbø is perhaps wondering about now what kind of hell he has signed up for as one of the Hammers’ youngest summer recruits.

However his is another fledgling career that looks to be hugely promising. Against Blackburn, the young winger looked prepared to take on and beat players in a way that his more seasoned colleague Manor Solomon appears to have forgotten.

Remember, West Ham were linked with Stoke City’s winger  Sorba Thomas in the summer – an ex Hammer who has in fact gone to Premier League Hull City and struggled enormously – so much so that footballleagueworld.co.uk claim ‘West Ham dodged huge £10.5 million transfer bullet’:

West Ham made a pretty shrewd decision by backing away from Sorba Thomas and investing in Edvin Austø

We may think things are bad right now, but with youngster Austbo West Ham look to have found a young talent with a high ceiling – compared with the -relatively speaking – wizened old pro’ Thomas who at 27 seems to have peaked, if Hull City’s experience is anything to go by. Good choice, Nils Koppen.

Very easy to hate on all things West Ham just now with the club sitting outside even the play off places. Austbø however continues to shine even on dark days at Ewood Park and needs to be nailed-on as a starter in place of Solomon who, by comparison, just looked plain ordinary.

From the old Bobby Moore Upper to the Billy Bonds' stand these days - I've been watching since '03 and a supporter since about 1970.. Favourite player - Dean Ashton: Curse you Shaun Wright-Phillips. I still watch YouTube repeats of the Cup Final of 2006 hoping in vain that Shaka Hislop grows another six inches and stops Steven Gerrard's injury time equaliser. Can tell I'm getting old knowing I watched both Mark Noble's debut and his last game at West Ham. Pulling on a Claret and Blue replica shirt still makes me feel the same butterflies as when I was seven years old. Magic.

The fans are the ones who are a credit to our club Weve proved our loyalty time and time again Waiting to see it from management owners and players

Credit for signing a player who has done what exactly in the second division so far? £20M on Engles, £5m on Solomon and £10m for Piroe had we gone up? I see nothing here to give him credit for. I was chatting to a guy Saturday who told me he thinks West Ham are the easiest team to play through in the league. He reckoned our midfield had zero defensive qualities and constantly left our back four exposed. The more I think about it, the more I see what he is saying. If we had no intention of playing Alvarez or Magassa, why didn’t we sign a midfielder who can defend or tackle because none of the current bunch can.

Promotion has to be the key aim this season, but it was always going to be a reset after the torrid few seasons and incompetent leadership at the club under Sullivan and his managers. I was ok with Nuno staying on, but hindsight always being clear 20/20 vision, I think it was Paco Jémez that was the factor in West Ham’s improvement towards the back end of last season. I hope Parker brings the feelgood factor back to the squad, last seen during the high times of Moyse. Stating the bleeding obvious, there’s still time to push for that automatic spot, but no room now for what we’ve been witnessing recently if it’s going to happen for us.

#2131. St Johnstone 2-1 Dundee: Hosts edge derby thriller with deflected winner

A deflected Kai Fotheringham strike on 72 minutes dealt Dundee their first defeat at St Johnstone for five years.

Josh Campbell scored the second headed goal of his loan from Hibernian to earn Saints a fifth-minute lead.

Substitute striker Joe Westley seized on a defensive howler to level just after halftime.

Fotheringham capped an excellent return from a two-match suspension to secure a 2-1 victory with his first goal since William Hill Premiership opening weekend.

Simo Valakari’s side won their fourth league game since returning to the top-flight and moved level on 17 points with their Tayside rivals.

Owen Bevan returned from injury to replace Joe Wright in Steven Pressley’s only change.

Reece McAlear’s illness forced Valakari into one of four switches that also included top-scorer Josh Fowler dropping to the bench.

Danny Schmidt recovered from an ankle knock to lead the line as Saints set the tone with a high-tempo and profitable opening spell.

Bosnian full-back Enes Alic swung over a terrific delivery to the near post. No Dundee defender was wise to the ghosting run of Campbell who arrived on cue to head emphatically past Owen Goodman.

Saints defender Bozo Mikulic was forced off with a facial knock on 14 minutes. Dan Finlayson replaced the Croatian and that defensive switch was not put under great strain in the first 45.

Dundee threatened only in the 24th minute when captain Ethan Hamilton’s surprise shot on the turn was diverted for a corner by Ross Sinclair.

Saints could easily have doubled their advantage three minutes before half-time. Alic conjured a fierce hit from 25 yards, parried out by Goodman. The rebound fell for Taylor Steven who snatched at the ball and shot well wide.

That missed opportunity came back to haunt the Saints quickly after the interval.

Finlayson ushered a header back towards Sinclair but, as the keeper came to gather, a collision with Cheick Diabate caused a spillage.

Westley, one of three halftime introductions, accepted the gift and found the empty net with ease. Saints, as they have done all season, responded well to a setback. Campbell went close at the near post and a full-stretch Goodman’s fingertips brushed a 30-yard dig from Cotterill just wide.

They wrested back the lead with a terrific transition move. Hamilton gave the ball away and Saints swiftly broke. After great work from Liam Smith down the right, Campbell’s blocked effort spun up for Fotheringham.

His shot took a heavy deflection to leave Goodman rooted to the spot as the ball sailed in.

Dundee had the ball in the net through Ryan Finnigan on 79 minutes. However, referee David Dickinson penalised Owen Bevan for a push in the penalty box melee.

And an offside flag denied Macaulay Tait a tap-in third for Saints. Dundee spurned one fine chance at an equaliser in stoppage time.

Westley scuffed his attempt from six yards, and Sinclair was relieved to gather.

#2130. ‘Standout performer’ Nick Woltemade adds to his stunning Juventus run

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Nick Woltemade continued his excellent Juventus form on Sunday night.

The Newcastle United loan star was a key player on Thursday in the Europa League when he got an assist for the winning goal away at AZ Alkmaar.

Nick Woltemade really finding his feet now after he only made one start for Juventus in the opening six weeks of his loan season after moving to Turin at the start of September.

Last night was only Big Nick’s third Serie A start and this trio of league matches all coming in the last fortnight.

Juventus trailed away at Fiorentina on Sunday night but 32 minutes on the clock Kolo Muani set up Nick Woltemade to equalise. Clever positioning getting the German international a bit of space away from his marker and a great right foot finish gave the keeper no chance.

Nick Woltemade was surprisingly subbed off as part of a double change on 57 minutes, probably due to how much football he has played in a short space of time after initially on the sidelines, Juventus went on to draw 2-2 last night against Fiorentina.

In the player ratings by Goal, Nick Woltemade was one of only two Juventus players to get an 8 out 10: ‘The standout performer in the final third, Woltemade scored the first equaliser in the 32nd minute. His link-up play was excellent before he was surprisingly withdrawn in the 57th minute as part of a double change.’

Despite only starting one competitive match at Juventus in his first six weeks at the club, Big Nick was bizarrely made the scapegoat for the poor start to the Juventus league season as they won only three of seven Serie A matches, none of which the Newcastle United loan star started…

Moving on, Juventus have now played 15 matches in all competitions.

The most recent of those games was last night.

Nick Woltemade has now started seven games in all competitions for Juventus and has six direct goal contributions, scoring four and getting two assists.

The overall Juventus results this season make stunning reading where Nick Woltemade is concerned, it is almost as though there is a pattern forming, Juventus unbeaten in the seven matches Big Nick has started and winning five of those seven.

It is also worth noting that the Newcastle United striker makes Juventus a far bigger threat in attack when playing, especially the way he links up play and creates chances and space for others.

Juventus have scored 17 goals in the seven matches Nick Woltemade has started (at least two goals in each of the seven), whilst in the eight games the NUFC player hasn’t been in the starting eleven they have only scored nine goals.

Juventus 2026-27 record in all competitions Played 15 Won 8 Drawn 4 Lost 3

Juventus 2026-27 record with Nick Woltemade starting Played 7 Won 5 Drawn 2 Lost 0

Juventus 2026-27 record with Nick Woltemade not starting Played 8 Won 3 Drawn 2 Lost 3

The real story of Nick Woltemade at Juventus is a little different to how the Italian and UK media have reported it. The Newcastle United loan star was recently voted October 2026 player of the month for Juventus.

Hopefully we will now see Nick Woltemade be a regular for Juventus in both Europe and Serie A. A successful loan season to help progress a striker who had made a very limited number of starts at top league level in Germany before joining Newcastle United. United would then have the choice of looking to get Big Nick back into the Newcastle United team, or alternatively getting a very healthy transfer fee to help finance other recruitment.

#2129. Now made public that first of the 2026-27 twenty Premier League managers is to be sacked

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Still no Premier League managers sacked so far this season BUT that is now set to change.

The Athletic reporting that their information is that Crystal Palace are now going to sack Pierre Sage.

We incredibly got past fireworks night with still none of the 20 Premier League managers getting fired, by this point last season a quartet of Premier League managers had lost their jobs by 6 November 2025 – Nuno, Graham Potter, Ange Postecoglou and Vitor Pereira. Eleven in total lost their jobs during the 2025-26 season.

International breaks are always a popular time for sacking Premier League managers with a bit of time to appoint a replacement before the league games resume.

We have now just gone past the 11 weeks of the season mark and The Athletic now state: ‘Crystal Palace are set to sack manager Pierre Sage after 16 games in charge. Palace suffered a 3-1 defeat by Liverpool at Selhurst Park on Sunday, leaving the south London side bottom of the Premier League table for the first time after a complete round of games since December 2017. Sage was appointed in June as Oliver Glasner’s replacement but has overseen just two wins in 10 Premier League games this season; Palace have the league’s worst defensive record, with 24 goals conceded so far.’

Crystal Palace have lost all of their last four Premier League games and conceded 12 goals in these matches, losing to Brighton, Newcastle United, Spurs and Liverpool. Only scoring once themselves and that was a penalty yesterday in the 95th minute when already 3-0 down to Liverpool.

As for a replacement, The Athletic report: ‘Palace will look to appoint Sage’s successor during the upcoming two-week international break, with names under consideration including Thomas Frank and Sean Dyche, who left their respective former clubs Tottenham Hotspur and Nottingham Forest in February. Vitor Pereira, who left Forest this summer, and Tony Popovic — the former centre-back who spent five seasons of his playing career at Palace and is currently in charge of Australia’s national team — are also potential successors. There is also admiration for Coventry City’s Frank Lampard.’

In total, eleven Premier League managers were sacked during last (2025-26) season (with their replacements in brackets):

9 September 2025 – Nuno leaves Forest (Ange Postecoglou) 27 September 2025 – Graham Potter leaves West Ham (Nuno) 18 October 2025 – Ange Postecoglou leaves Forest (Sean Dyche) 2 November 2025 – Vitor Pereira leaves Wolves (Rob Edwards) 1 January 2026 – Enzo Maresca leaves Chelsea (Liam Rosenior) 5 January 2026 – Ruben Amorim leaves Man U (Michael Carrick) 11 February 2026 – Thomas Frank leaves Spurs (Igor Tudor) 12 February 2026 – Sean Dyche leaves Forest (Vitor Pereira) 29 March 2026 – Igor Tudor leaves Spurs (Roberto de Zerbi) 22 April 2026 – Liam Rosenior leaves Chelsea (Caretaker boss for rest of season) 30 April 2026 – Scott Parker leaves Burnley (Caretaker boss for rest of season)

Premier League table on Monday 9 November 2026

A defeat this weekend for any of the Premier League managers most at risk was sure to put them in immediate danger.

Forest beat Man City, Sunderland won at home against Chelsea to lift them up to second bottom, that would have been third bottom but Michael Carrick fluked a point from a bizarre 4-4 draw with Villa.

So Pierre Sage and Crystal Palace the only ones towards the bottom to lose this weekend and that seemingly sealing the Palace manager’s fate. 🎙️ THE MAG PODCAST Ep 13: Newcastle United beat Palace, Schar and Burn Deliver, and Eddie Howe to Man Utd? #2128. Wily veterans and the fountain of youth: The five key battles in Milan vs. Ferencvaros

AC Milan return to Europa League action at San Siro this evening for a must-win game against high-flyers Ferencvaros.

Starting their European campaign with two defeats (vs. Benfica and Bournemouth) and one win last left Milan down in 24th in the table, meaning that they need to turn things around if they are to mount a surge towards the top eight spots.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Tonight’s game will be far from straightforward though, as Ferencvaros have taken nine points from nine and therefore sit fourth in the table. They are 20 unbeaten across all competitions and are two points from the summit in their domestic league, with a game in hand to play.

Reports are suggesting that Ruben Amorim will turn to a youthful line-up for this one despite the status of being a must-win game. However, the spine of the team will still be made up of players who must deliver.

Starting with a rather unconventional battle, the one between the two goalkeepers Lorenzo Torriani and Dénes Dibusz could be potentially decisive, for obvious reasons. Ferencvaros have conceded just three goals in their three Europa games so far and just 10 in 10 in the league, and the 35-year-old veteran Dibusz has been a big part of that, even if there has been some rotation.

For Torriani, this is arguably his biggest opportunity in a Milan shirt. His only other start came in a Coppa Italia rout of Sassuolo, while he came off the bench in a Champions League defeat to Liverpool, and in the Bournemouth defeat. This is a huge chance for the 20-year-old to not only show he is a capable deputy in the present, but a potential Mike Maignan successor down the line.

There will also be two crucial duels involving the two Nagys, Oliver and Adam. The former will play at right-back and faces the difficult task of keeping Alphadjo Cisse quiet. The Italian is the Rossoneri’s top scorer this season and will be champing at the bit to build on his hat-trick against RB Salzburg. Oliver Nagy is dangerous going forward though, with two assists in his five starts, so Cisse will have to help out defensively too.

Adam Nagy meanwhile faces the task of stopping Milan’s second-top scorer, Adrien Rabiot. The Frenchman netted his fifth of the season in the derby against Inter, and Amorim has chosen to rely on his experience against an opponent who is also 31 years of age. The Hungarian signed from Spezia in the summer and is best known for his appearances at the 2016, 2020 and 2024 UEFA European Championships for his national team.

Ferencvaros have two main threats that Milan must keep quiet, especially the way that this game could play out with the visitors no doubt keen to contain and counter. Bamidele Yusuf is the first, and the Nigerian is expected to start up front this evening though he can also play and drift wide. He has six goals and three assists in 10 starts this season for the green and whites.

Bamidele Yusuf 🎯#UEL | @Fradi_HU pic.twitter.com/AXnt4XPaSu

— UEFA Europa League (@EuropaLeague) October 29, 2026

Sanhoun Diawara will have to do his bit to keep Yusuf quiet, but our feeling is that Koni De Winter will take on the man-marking duties just like he did with Inter’s lone striker Marcus Thuram in the derby. The Belgian has been undroppable in a literal sense, so we hope that no signs of fatigue are seen especially in transition, like against Bologna.

The visitors’ other danger man is Kristoffer Zachariassen, who matches Yusuf on nine goal contributions (seven goals, two assists) for the season. The 32-year-old Norwegian has plenty of experience and an eye for goal from the attacking midfield role, though his heat maps show he tends to drift to the right too.

So, it will be down to Ardon Jashari to keep tabs on him. Amorim and Milan are still waiting for the Swiss to put together a good run of solid starts after his arrival from Club Brugge for over €30m, and this is the kind of game that he needs to seize control of and dominate to show he is capable of being the anchor man, especially with Luka Modric’s retirement surely not far away.

#2127. Scott Parker Has a Selection Dilemma and the Numbers Are Damning

Plenty has already been written about Mads Hermansen, with transfer speculation continuing to swirl. Reports suggest Newcastle’s Nick Pope could be a target when the January window opens, but for now, West Ham’s goalkeeping situation remains firmly under the spotlight.

The numbers are difficult to ignore. A goalkeeper who isn’t making enough saves and is shipping goals at an alarming rate, 23 conceded in 15 games, is becoming a problem that cannot be overlooked.

One possible solution could be Alphonse Areola, who previously worked under Scott Parker at Fulham. There is also a potential opportunity for highly-rated youngster Finlay Herrick, who may be worth a closer look.

While Areola’s statistics last season hardly inspire confidence, conceding 37 goals in 20 appearances without recording a clean sheet, there is at least some context. By comparison, Hermansen managed seven clean sheets while conceding 28 goals in 18 matches.

The pair offer very different strengths and weaknesses! Areola is arguably the better shot-stopper but struggles when asked to play out from the back. Hermansen, meanwhile, has been preferred for his distribution and comfort in possession, yet questions remain over his save percentage and ability to keep the ball out of the net when it matters most.

Ex-Goalie Nuno failed to get the best out of Hermansen

Another concern is the absence of an established senior goalkeeping coach. That said, it’s worth remembering that the club’s former manager was a goalkeeper himself, while Rui Barbosa brought years of coaching and playing experience. Neither appeared able to significantly influence Hermansen’s development.

Currently, Billy Lepine, a former Dagenham & Redbridge youth player who has worked within the academy setup since 2008, occupies the role. Lukasz Fabianski is also assisting on a part-time basis with the academy.

And perhaps that’s where the story takes an even stranger twist.

Cast your mind back to 4th December 2024, when West Ham travelled to the King Power Stadium. Leicester won 3-1, ending a six-game winless run. On that night, West Ham peppered the Leicester goal with 31 shots, the highest number they had ever recorded in a Premier League match. Ten were on target and they dominated possession with 61%.

Standing between the posts for Leicester that evening?

None other than Mads Hermansen, who produced a performance worthy of Middle-earth, adopting Gandalf’s famous stance of “You shall not pass!” as he admirably defended his goal.

The previous year in the Championship he featured in the EFL team of the season. One of the most proactive ball playing keepers in the league, and completed 13 clean sheets.

If ever there was evidence of the “West Ham goalkeeper curse”, that might just be it.

The solution feels fairly straightforward. Bring Fabianski into the senior goalkeeping coaching setup, get Areola focused solely on football rather than the DJ decks, and bring in an experienced goalkeeper on loan in January to provide competition.

The ball is now firmly in Scott Parker’s court.

I have been a season ticket holder since the late eighties, so experienced the highs and lows of being a West Ham supporter. I previously wrote for OLAS and have contributed to a number of football publications in the past.

A top goalkeeper and a striker should be our priority in January

Now I am not saying Hermansen shouldn’t be relieved of his duties — he should be replaced.

However, last season’s Stats shout out what problems our Goalkeepers face ….. Areloa played his matches with Dinos and Dumbo, whoops sorry, Kilman in front if him, whilst tge majority of Hermansen’s matches had Dinos and Disasi.

Replace Kilman and whichever goalkeeper is in between the Hammers sticjs, will have improved Stats

Does Fabianski still have his boots and gloves? Seriously Herrick is much better at playing out from the back than the other two, he just seems lacking in height for me. Would he dominate his area in a way we have been calling out for this season?

Our “goalkeeper curse” is nothing compared to our “striker curse”.

“Bernd Leno (Fulham): Unbelievable couple of saves from him to keep Fulham in the game. I thought Newcastle should have been three or four up before Fulham got the equaliser.”

Lukas Hornicek made some smart saves but United had comfortably more clear chances and could/should have won the game if not for the excellence of Bernd Leno. Though even he could do nothing about Jacob Murphy’s stunner.

#2125. Report claims winter move could rescue West Ham player from year-long ordeal in east London

There’s increasing consternation that some of the signings from last season are proving inadequate even for this, the second division of English football. This site’s opinions over Pablo Julio are well known and well documented – the bearded one is a trier but still plays as if he’s a member of the crowd who’s won a lucky programme raffle to play with the big boys each time he appears in a West Ham shirt.

Perhaps even more concerning is Taty Castellanos’ failure to make any impact whatsoever on this West Ham side following relegation. The Argentine attacker has just one goal to his name this season – from memory his yellow cards now out score his goals – and he merely struts around looking angry each time he’s called upon without contributing significantly to the team output. How the recruitment team will be wishing they’d cashed-in on the reported £40 million Everton interest on deadline day.

Options may be on the horizon for a January exit – it appears Taty still has his admirers: Sportwitness.co.uk make the claim:

“River Plate have identified West Ham United‘s Valentín Castellanos as the ‘top target’ for the winter market as part of their plan to strengthen their attack.

His contract lasts until 2030, with an option for another year, and Transfermarkt value him at €28m. The frontman’s contract and salary he earns with Scott Parker’s side are the ‘main obstacles’ for River Plate.

Therefore, the Argentine club are considering alternatives like signing him on loan with a fee or buying a percentage of his rights. This is only possible if the London club were to give their approval.”

Whether there’s any real mileage in the River Plate interest, it may well be that West Ham at least have a bargaining chip to try and negotiate a sale of Castellanos in January which would more than likely suit player and club. Taty can then find a league in which his talents are more suited and West Ham can source a front man which will better  suit Scott Parker’s playing style.

From the old Bobby Moore Upper to the Billy Bonds' stand these days - I've been watching since '03 and a supporter since about 1970.. Favourite player - Dean Ashton: Curse you Shaun Wright-Phillips. I still watch YouTube repeats of the Cup Final of 2006 hoping in vain that Shaka Hislop grows another six inches and stops Steven Gerrard's injury time equaliser. Can tell I'm getting old knowing I watched both Mark Noble's debut and his last game at West Ham. Pulling on a Claret and Blue replica shirt still makes me feel the same butterflies as when I was seven years old. Magic.

Both Nuno picks I believe which is terrible considering his PL and Championship experience levels. That on top of his limited tactical ability. His success at Wolves is ancient history now and the Forest escapade looks a solitary season in that light. It’s going to be a desperate club wherever he coaches next.

We’ve made appalling recruitments Martin, how bad must they be when they can’t even succeed at this level. Amortisation and loan fees get us out of jail and we rarely make a loss on the books, but it’s the lack of contribution that has killed us. We’ve invested a Kings ransom in players who have done us no good on the pitch is why we’re languishing where we are. Frankly it beggars any belief how awful our recruitment has been.

#2124. First Newcastle United match of the Premier League season but hopefully not the last

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

The first live Premier League Newcastle United match of the season for us.

Albeit sat in the supposed home supporters end at Craven Cottage.

I wake up early to a London pea souper. By midday the mist is starting to lift and we are on the train to Putney.

It is then a walk across Putney Bridge to Archbishop’s Park. It is on this walk over the bridge where we see our first half and half scarf. Oh dear.

After a few beers with our Fulham friends it is off to Craven Cottage which is wedged between the river and streets of beautiful Victorian housing. A classic example of a football club from a different era and hemmed in from that time.

Through the turnstiles at the rear of the Cottage and then we are in our seats in row ZZ, the back row to be precise.

I have been in the Putney end many times but on this occasion there appears to be fewer black and white stripes on show than previously. But significantly there is a lot of half and half scarves. An awful creation which has a crest with the words Geordie Boys inside it.

We stand during the minute’s silence for Remembrance Day and a young man and his partner take their seats in the row in front of us talking loudly, mobile phones in hands. A woman turns around and tells them to “shut up and show some respect.”

We start the game brightly but it turns into another game like Palace. The highlight is the Dan Burn goal which we celebrate but are completely baffled at it being disallowed as we have probably got the worst seats in the house to make any reasoned judgement.

Twenty minutes into the game and groups of people start leaving their seats, some wearing half and halfs. This cycle goes on throughout the game, small groups moving in and out. Other spectators stand up and start recording with their phones, or taking selfies, blocking our line of sight as the game is happening.

At this moment I realise now why my Chelsea mates are so vexed, as this is what they have described to me, but even worse for them as it is happening in their main end, the Matthew Harding stand.

No wonder they are angry. I was getting angry and we were in the Fulham end.

Second half we start brightly and I am hopeful for another Palace-like after the break performance.

Before the game my son had said “I am going home if Jacob Murphy starts”, so down on the winger he is.

A big Geordie lad has spotted us and the adjacent tourist seat that has been vacated, he joins us. We have the perfect view of the Murphy goal and we celebrate like we were in the Gallowgate End.

Three minutes later and you are reminded of what it is to be a Newcastle United fan.

The trudge through the park back to Putney station, me and my lad debate how poor the referee was and the reasons for it.

First Newcastle United match of the Premier League season but hopefully not the last.

#2122. The tactical 'freedom' Celtic give Callum Osmand and his unlikely Camilo Duran bond

With Celtic a goal behind against Besiktas in the 60th minute, on came Callum Osmand. His impact was almost instantaneous, equalising with his first touch and, soon after, setting up fellow substitute Camilo Duran with a refined reverse pass.

Martin O'Neill said it was all part of the masterplan. The Celtic manager rotated his XI heavily before calling on the cavalry come the hour.

Osmand's influence on the 3-2 victory was profound. He enthused the home support with fresh attacking impetus, haring at Besiktas' defence and providing that crucial end product.

Although Osmand averages a goal or assist every 90 minutes this season, he concedes he must improve.

"I would say I'm nowhere near where I want to be personally, and there's stuff I need to tidy up on, decision-making and all this stuff," Osmand said. "But I feel like the more games I play, the more I understand and the more I learn.

"So on a personal note, that's what I want to do, just keep learning and keep understanding my role, like the team and obviously the players you're playing with.

"And I've still only played a handful of games, so it's tough learning, but I feel like when you get thrown in at the deep end, it's the best way to learn, and the worst games are what you learn off more than the good games.

"It's just as long as I can get better every game, that's all I really want to focus on."

Osmand joined Celtic from Fulham last summer as a central striker, yet since the defeat to Benfica last month, he's been moulded into a left winger.

Learning a new position isn't easy, though Osmand likes the freedom that comes with playing out wide.

"It is new for me, but I'm really enjoying it," he said. "It's a really fun position and it's very, very attacking.

"I have a lot of freedom and the staff give me that freedom and tell me to go and try and make something happen. So it's a great feeling when you know you can just go and sort of impose your game."

Osmand did exactly that on Thursday evening. O'Neill told him to 'just go' before coming on, instructing the 20-year-old to bring the energy that gets supporters on their feet.

"I think that's the best feeling in football, when you can get everyone behind you and it feels amazing, so that's what I sort of strive for, that feeling," Osmand said.

His presence helped flip the game on its head, offering Celtic fresh hope of Europa League progression after defeats to Ferencvaros, Benfica, and Celta Vigo.

O'Neill's side can look ahead to their trip to Torreense later this month knowing it means something.

"For us, it felt like a must win, that was our sort of mindset going into that. This was sort of it," Osmand said of the Besiktas game. "Like we knew we could still qualify, but we knew we had to get something out of Thursday night, and I think the boys done amazing, so hopefully we just get some confidence and build on from this.

"We have some tougher away ties, but hopefully we can use that and just use this, and that gives us confidence to play more free, and take more risks.

"Sometimes when you're not as confident, it's tough to play the football you want to play, but as you can see, when we're confident, it just goes forward every time, and it's a good feeling, so hopefully we can build on that."

For Celtic, wins like Thursday's have proven rare this season. There was a real sense of togetherness at the full-time whistle.

O'Neill raised his right fist to the heavens in celebration before gracing the turf and embracing his players.

Osmand knows Celtic haven't been at their best of late. Last weekend's defeat at Falkirk sparked some all too familiar emotions.

Thursday sent Celtic to the other end of the spectrum. Now they must stay there.

"I think we know that we're a good side," Osmand said. "We all back each other, and I think when we're all together, and the fans are with us, and you feel it, you just want to get everyone sort of on one page, and then we feel like an amazing team.

"It's sometimes tough to get to that point, because we're lacking confidence, or we're not playing as well, but I think Thursday night really showed everyone was together, and the final whistle gave us that. It should give us that confidence to go on."

Osmand dovetailed superbly with Duran after coming on against Besiktas, setting up the Colombian striker's first goal of the triumph.

That relationship extends beyond the pitch, even if a language barrier remains.

On Duran, Osmand said: "He's unbelievable, a really top player. You can just see even by the way he walks and the way he moves.

"I learn off him every day. He's an amazing guy.

"His English is really not great, but somehow we manage to talk to each other a lot. I think I find him quite a good friend of mine now.

"And although we might not speak many words, you can tell just by looking... I don't know how to describe it. Like we talk to each other a lot. Maybe it's little words, but I feel like we get on really well. He's a great guy."

You wouldn't bet against Duran and Osmand once again coming to the fore when Celtic host Kilmarnock in the William Hill Premiership on Sunday afternoon.

The champions defeated Neil McCann's side 5-1 at Rugby Park back in August. A similar result would go a long way to building on the positive feeling triggered by Thursday's victory.

"I think sometimes when you don't give a team that's obviously not doing as well respect, then you can get caught, and sometimes you don't want to get too overconfident going into these games, because then you'll get caught out," Osmand added.

"I think it's just giving every team you play respect, and knowing that most teams can hurt us, and we have to just go in with the same mentality as Thursday night, and hopefully get a good result.

"I think it's really important for the league. Obviously, we're still at the top of the league, but obviously the gap can change at any time, so it's just about winning every game possible in the league, and just building on everything."
