#2080. Crass Steven Gerrard claim leaves Celtic hero unhappy as he sets him straight

Former Celtic goalkeeper Joe Hart has taken issue with Steven Gerrard over the former Rangers boss’ brutal assessment of Gianluigi Donnarumma.

The two former Old Firm star turns have found themselves on opposite sides of a goalkeeping debate after ex-Rangers manager Gerrard likened Manchester City No.1 Donnarumma to a “wet Weetabix” while criticising his recent performances. Hart has now hit back at that description and explained why he believes the Italian’s struggles need.

Hart, speaking on Overlap Daily, said: “The job’s not to save everything, because there are so many hindsight goalkeepers, and I hear them all the time and I understand it. I heard people talking about it. I think Stevie G was talking on here and he used a term about Donnarumma which didn’t make me happy. It didn’t feel right, and I would never do that.

“No, no, I love Stevie. Stevie’s awesome and he knows that. But it’s just my goalkeeping. I think goalkeeping is special. My protective blanket came on when he talked about Donnarumma being one-on-one against Aston Villa and Nicholas Jackson.

“If you’re on that angle and you want to make it as difficult as you can for someone to beat you, you can’t afford to stand on that tight angle. You can’t afford to have your hands up here because the easiest finish is the wrap-around. So you almost have to say, ‘If you want to beat me, you’ve got it.’

Read more: Banishing the Rangers 'hoodoo' - key man reveals dressing room plan to fix it

“You rarely see someone thrashing it. You’ll see a goal where they flail at it, but it’s the hardest finish because you’ve got the least control. The top players can curl it, they can smash it, they can get their head over the ball. As we hear everyone talking about, lift your head and lean back. It’s not an easy finish.

“Jackson got one to about here, and then Gvardiol had a similar moment against Suzuki in the second half. His hands were low and it was probably just about head height, and he had the speed and timing to get his hands here rather than there, and he flicked it onto the bar.

“There are tiny little bits that come into goalkeeping, about making it as difficult as you possibly can. With Donnarumma at the moment, I think he went a little bit away from that. He was trying to help the team rather than just be the top goalkeeper that he is.”

#2079. What Trey Nyoni did just before Alexander Isak goal isn’t getting enough attention

Trey Nyoni’s rise at Liverpool this season has been impressive.

The youngster’s potential was obvious to Andoni Iraola’s predecessor, Arne Slot, last term, but the club rightly decided to be careful with what was an 18-year-old footballer with limited senior experience.

It’s very much a different story in 2026/27, however, with the Basque head coach having already handed the midfielder over 600 minutes of action across the Premier League, Champions League and Carabao Cup.

If three consecutive starts for Liverpool – against Chelsea, Arsenal and Fenerbahce – doesn’t prove it, you have to think that the nature of Nyoni’s introduction against Crystal Palace more or less seals the view that Nyoni has become a key player for Iraola.

The correct decision was made ahead of time to rest the former Leicester City prodigy after a flurry of games, with our player of the season last year, Dominik Szoboszlai, restored to the starting XI.

But when it came time for the Hungarian to depart the pitch due to an injury concern, it was Trey Nyoni the manager turned to at the 69th minute mark. Yes, it’s worth pointing out that senior midfielders (other than Wataru Endo) aren’t exactly running amok on the Liverpool bench at this point in time. But this felt like a trusted substitution, a body Iraola has come to rely on, rather than one that just had to be made.

The assist credit will go to Florian Wirtz for the Alexander Isak goal close to full time, but it would be remiss of us to overlook Trey Nyoni’s contribution moments before.

The teenager can be spotted cutting out a low cross from Tyrick Mitchell in the box before picking out Alexander Isak (surrounded by three Palace players) further up the pitch. The ball plays out to Victor Munoz on the right flank, and Liverpool find a Palace defence in absolute disarray.

Isak strikes late on 💪🇸🇪 pic.twitter.com/J2fHbXlZyD

It’s not a fancy crossfield pass or Hollywood Gerrard ball, but there’s intention behind it, and it’s a positive use of the ball to help kickstart a Liverpool counter. Exactly what Andoni Iraola wants to see his midfielders doing at Liverpool on a frequent basis.

Ultimately, it’s so encouraging to see Nyoni continuing to be impactful in games even when he’s coming on, effectively, to see things out.

#2078. Inglorious Hearts crash as flying Falkirk dismantle Wouter Vrancken's toiling Jambos

Rampant Falkirk obliterated Hearts’ 18-month unbeaten home record in the William Hill Premiership with a stunning 5-2 win at Tynecastle as they leapfrogged the Jambos into third place.

Wouter Vrancken’s beleaguered side, missing 11 players through injury amid a gruelling fixture list, were in disarray as the swashbuckling Bairns romped into a five-goal lead early in the second half through Finley Barbrook, Owen Eames, Liam Henderson and Jacob Murrell’s double.

Hearts hit back through substitute Sabri Guendouz and a Claudio Braga penalty, but Falkirk were well worthy of making it five top-flight wins in a row for the first time since 1995.

It was a first league defeat at Tynecastle for Hearts since April 2025. To exacerbate their grim predicament, the Jambos, who have won just two of their last 11 matches, lost yet another senior player as Malachi Fagan-Walcott limped off in the second half.

There were two changes to the Hearts side that started Thursday’s Conference League defeat to Thun as Stephen Kingsley and Guendouz were replaced by Yan Dhanda and Landry Kabore.

Read more: Furious Aberdeen fans demand Stephen Robinson axe amid miserable form

Falkirk boss John McGlynn, named manager of the month for October, made one enforced change from the side that defeated Celtic last Sunday as Jack McMillan took over from injured right-back Ryan Strain.

The Bairns seized the lead in the fourth minute. After Murrell’s close-range effort from Scott Tanser’s cross was brilliantly saved by Beau Reus, Barbrook reacted quickest to drill home a low, angled finish from eight yards out.

Hearts threatened an equaliser in the 10th minute, but Kabore’s effort on the turn from the edge of the six-yard box was superbly blocked by Scott Bain.

Falkirk doubled their lead in the 17th minute after the hosts were caught wide open on the counter-attack. Dhanda’s shot from distance was charged down, allowing the Bairns to break swiftly, with Brad Spencer weighting his pass perfectly for Eames, who fired past the exposed Reus.

Braga thought he had pulled one back for Hearts in the 20th minute, but it was ruled out for handball.

Falkirk took full advantage of this reprieve by adding a third in the 33rd minute as Murrell peeled off Fagan-Walcott at the back post to nod home Deniss Melniks’ cross from the right.

The visitors struck again in first-half stoppage-time as Henderson curled high past Reus after Tanser’s corner broke to him just inside the box.

As jeers rained down from an irate home support, Vrancken replaced midfielders Laurent Mendy and Dhanda with Guendouz and Matthew Gillies for the start of the second half.

But within two minutes of the restart Falkirk notched again as Murrell fired home after being set up by Ethan Ross.

Hearts got off the mark when Guendouz drilled in his first goal for the club from just inside the box in the 50th minute.

Braga then tucked away a penalty in the 74th minute after Guendouz was tripped by Lewis Neilson, but it was not enough to prevent a third straight defeat for the Jambos.

#2077. 'It's awful' - Expert shares what Chelsea hierarchy think of Xabi Alonso after defeat to Sunderland

Chelsea are unlikely to hold any major concerns about Xabi Alonso despite their inconsistent results in recent weeks.

The 44-year-old has faced backlash from sections of the supporters at Stamford Bridge, who have questions his team selections, substitutions, and his tactical approach.

A 1-0 defeat against Sunderland last time out, who were bottom of the Premier League table before kickoff, has once again seen fans asking questions of the boss.

However, former Man United chief scout Mick Brown told Football Insider that Alonso is held in extremely high regard behind the scenes at Chelsea and is being backed for success.

Chelsea have no immediate concerns about the manager's recent record, despite what has been an inconsistent start, and they hope results will improve as the season goes on.

Alonso's side have won five, drawn one and lost four of their first ten Premier League games, but currently sit fifth in the table, and are hopeful of further improvements.

Brown told Football Insider on 26 October that Chelsea are hopeful Alonso could be the man to lead them to success and are prepared to give him time to improve.

Instead, there are more concerns about the players and their inconsistency which has led to some mixed results in the early stages of the new manager's tenure.

Alonso has been clear that this Chelsea side is not the same one we will see come the end of the season, and he is being backed by the board for long-term success.

"I don't think Chelsea have any major worries about Xabi Alonso at the moment," Brown told Football Insider.

"Chelsea fans have high expectations, they want to be winning every week and they want to be winning silverware, so whenever they lose a game there is a lot of noise.

"A defeat against Sunderland will be a bit of a worry, of course, because when you look at where they are in the table compared to where Chelsea want to be, it's an awful result.

"Chelsea's biggest problem is their consistency, they can win 5-0 one week and then go and lose 1-0 the next, but that's on the players just as much as the manager.

"I think Alonso is being backed to turn things around, and they want him to be in charge for a long time, because they think he can lead them to success.

"So whether or not the fans are a bit frustrated, I don't think it really matters, because the club are happy with what they've seen from Alonso."

Alonso still has the backing of the Chelsea board despite a mixed start to the season so far, but the fans have begun to express their frustrations, largely via social media.

Questions have been asked of his tactical decisions and player selections, which was raised as an issue again following the 1-0 defeat to Sunderland.

Meanwhile, Football Insider reported on 29 October that Alonso's public comments have also left Chelsea fans angry after he dismissed the importance of the League Cup.

A penalty shoot-out defeat against Liverpool saw Chelsea bow out of the tournament, but the manager insisted it was not a priority, with focus on other competitions.

With no European football and a very unlikely chance of winning the Premier League, Alonso is now running out of ways to win a trophy in his first season.

#2076. AC Milan 0-2 Ferencvaros: Rossoneri fall to another dire Europa League defeat

AC Milan fell to a third Europa League defeat in four games as they were beaten 2-0 at home by Ferencvaros.

The hero of the night for the Hungarian side was without doubt Lenny Joseph, who netted twice in the second half to capitalise firstly on a loose touch from Lorenzo Torriani and then from a two-on-one break.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

A red card for the substitute Yusif threatened to change the momentum of the game, but the Rossoneri were unable to fashion any real response to put the result in doubt in what was another forgettable European night.

The result means that Milan have now dropped out of even the top 24 spots, and they can just about say goodbye to any hopes of direct last-16 qualification barring a miracle.

Ruben Amorim chose to make six changes from the team that beat Inter in the derby, with Lorenzo Torriani, Filippo Terracciano, Davide Bartesaghi, Ardon Jashari, Omari Hutchinson and Alphadjo Cisse coming into the team.

Ferencvaros started the game on top and they created the first big chance of the game less than four minutes in. A loose pass as Milan tried to build out was seized upon by Zachariassen who threaded Joseph through, and though his initial attempt was blocked by Koni De Winter, the forward managed to get another shot off from a few yards out that was thankfully straight at Torriani.

The first 15 minutes were quite frankly dreadful from Milan, in complete contrast to the victory at the weekend. The away side dominated possession thanks to so many sloppy giveaways, and Birmancevic nearly found himself bearing down on goal in a central area though he fired at his own man after some good close control.

It continued to be all the Hungarian side as the majority of the San Siro crowd began to grow worried and impatient. Another shot towards the goal came in the 17th minute, and even if Zachariassen did roll it straight at Torriani the fact he was found in space beyond the defensive line caused more worry.

Milan did not grow into the game as hoped and the errors kept coming. A stray pass backwards from Jashari under pressure put Joseph through on goal for Ferencvaros, though Torriani read his shot towards the bottom right corner well and was able to claim it. Another warning sign, however.

The first half was probably best summarised by two fouls in quick succession. The first saw Cisse act on the frustration of losing the ball and go lunging in to earn a yellow card that in fairness to the youngster was harsh, then Bartesaghi lost possession near the touchline before clumsily bundling his man over to give away a free-kick.

It took until the 39th minute for Milan to have their first shot of the game, but Cisse lashed it well over the bar from an Adrien Rabiot knock-down that landed nicely just beyond the penalty spot. At the other end, Joseph got the better of Diawara to surge into the box, yet Torriani was equal to his effort from a very narrow angle.

Torriani was by far the busier of the two goalkeepers and he was called into action again a few minutes from the break, with Joseph again the man who found space to shoot inside the box. The Italian got a strong hand to thwart the angled drive.

Amorim was clearly very displeased with what he saw in the first half, as he chose to make three changes at the break, bringing on Mario Gila, Diego Moreira and Christian Pulisic. Diawara, Cisse and Yunus Musah were the ones to come off.

Milan started the second half the better of the two sides, with Hutchinson firing into the side netting and then Ramos going on a winding run past three players into the box before a deflected shot.

Seven minutes into the second half, the deadlock was finally broken and it was unfortunately a moment to forget for Torriani. De Winter played a bit of a demanding pass back to the goalkeeper inside the box and the heavy first touch was seized upon, with the Ferencvaros player going down for what would have been a penalty had Joseph not been on hand to slot into an empty net.

The Rossoneri’s response was almost instant with Ramos again at the centre of some good work on the edge of the box, feeding Hutchinson’s run beyond the last man down the left side of the box, though the shot across goal just rolled wide of the far post.

In the 66th minute, Ferencvaros dealt Milan a sucker punch as they doubled their advantage just after Jashari had come off for Luka Modric. A bit of a ricochet in midfield led to a dangerous two-on-one situation for the visitors, allowing Zachariassen to lay it on a plate to Joseph, who simply had to slot it into an empty net.

The final change came just after with Francesco Camarda coming on for Bartesaghi, and he was not far from reopening the contest with a near-post flick from Moreira’s cross. Up the other end, a quickly taken free-kick saw Zachariassen’s half-volley draw a reaction save from Torriani.

There was a moment of madness from the substitute Yusuf with 15 minutes left on the clock as he seemed to reach out an elbow to strike Gila unprovoked. The Spaniard went down, VAR took a look and the referee sent him off.

Dibusz hadn’t been very busy all night, but the veteran goalkeeper was called upon to make a good save with his legs from Hutchinson’s shot through a crowd. It was looking more and more like not being the Diavolo’s night.

Ferencvaros should have had a third in the second of four added minutes when another loose pass towards Torriani was collected by Madarasz, who rounded the keeper but hit the side-netting.

#2075. “I’m really upset” – One thing hugely annoyed Andoni Iraola despite Liverpool win on Sunday

Andoni Iraola was left ‘really upset’ after Liverpool’s win over Crystal Palace on Sunday despite the positive, morale-boosting result for his team.

Having begun November with defeats to Arsenal and Fenerbahce, the Reds went to Selhurst Park in search of a pick-me-up in their final game prior to the international window, and they duly got in the form of a 3-1 victory.

Goals from Alexis Mac Allister, Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak had the points secured well before a stoppage-time penalty when, in a clash of heads between Milos Kerkez and Dario Osorio, the Hungarian was deemed to be the perpetrator and referee Tony Harrington pointed to the spot.

Eddie Nketiah converted from 12 yards to deny Liverpool a fifth Premier League clean sheet of the campaign, and speaking to Sky Sports shortly after the final whistle, Iraola’s frustration over the awarding of the penalty was clear.

The Basque said: “I’m very upset [with] what they are calling in our box penalties, and the ones they’re not calling in the other box. I know that we are 3-0, it’s the 95th minute, but I’m very upset.

“It’s a head-to-head but even Osorio’s head, after touching the ball, is the one going to Milos. It’s not Milos to Osorio. A clash of heads.

“OK, you can say 3-0, 95 minutes, nothing happens, but for me there is more than this. There is more because it’s not the first time this season and you compare and I’m really upset, yes.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Thankfully the decision came at a point in the match where it had no bearing on the overall result, although we can still see why it put a dampener on the victory for Iraola.

To us, it seemed like a 50-50 contest between Kerkez and Osorio, with both players making a genuine attempt to win the ball and unfortunate to have clashed heads – most importantly, both were fine after the collision.

Harrington’s call didn’t have any major impact in the overall context of the day, but we take the Liverpool head coach’s point about the apparent inconsistency in terms of what referees deem to be a penalty and what they don’t.

There was certainly a far stronger case for a spot kick in our defeat to Arsenal last weekend when Jurrien Timber blatantly tugged Isak’s shirt inside the box, but somehow none of the officials on duty thought it was a foul.

It didn’t hurt the Reds yesterday, but hopefully on another occasion where there’s a stoppage-time penalty given in a game which is in the balance, we won’t end up having to talk about Iraola’s side being wronged by the referee and VAR.

#2073. Rangers hero Scott Arfield takes plunge into management with new player-boss role

Former Rangers star Scott Arfield has been appointed the new player-manager of East Fife.

The former Canada international has replaced Dick Campbell, with the Fifers currently languishing ninth in League One.

The 38-year-old spent the final weeks of last season as Livingston's interim boss but will now get the chance to properly launch his managerial career at Bayview.

Arfield spent five seasons with Rangers between 2018 and 2023, making more than 200 appearances for the Ibrox club.

“I am absolutely delighted to be the new manager of East Fife and I cannot wait to get started,” said Arfield, who has signed a contract until May 2029.

Read more: Dan Neil names Rangers' 'most important' trait as title momentum builds

“I feel I am ready to go into coaching after learning a lot from excellent managers during my playing career, and I am grateful to East Fife for believing in me and for giving me this opportunity.

“My aim is now to create opportunities for others and to build a team which will excite East Fife supporters and attract the attention of the local community.

“It is a highly respected club which has great potential, and it is a privilege to be given the chance to lead it forward.”

East Fife chairman Liam Anderson said: “We are delighted to have agreed a deal with Scott to become our new player-manager.

“This is an innovative appointment and gives a clear indication of our ambitions going forward.

“I am sure that the arrival of Scott will be welcomed by our fans, who are keen to see an exciting brand of football at Bayview.”

#2072. Liam Scales strike enough to drag Celtic across line in Kilmarnock win

Liam Scales provided a looping finish to earn Celtic a 1-0 victory over Kilmarnock.

The Irish defender hooked a Camilo Duran cross into the top corner in the 26th minute to restore Celtic’s four-point lead in the William Hill Premiership.

Celtic – and Kasper Hogh in particular – otherwise had a frustrating day in front of goal, with Benjamin Nygren missing a second-half penalty.

Hogh had an early goal disallowed as his barren run without a goal hit the 16-game mark since he netted a hat-trick at Kilmarnock on his second appearance.

The Danish striker finished from seven yards after being set up by Nygren and ran to the standing section to celebrate.

His joy was short-lived as referee John Beaton was summoned to the monitor and gave a free-kick to Killie for Mika Baur’s challenge on Greg Kiltie.

Killie had some good first-half chances and Celtic could not get the two-goal cushion in a dominant second half.

The champions were nearly made to pay in stoppage time, but Ieuan Owen could not make any contact with Erik Ring’s inviting cross inside the six-yard box.

Celtic manager Martin O’Neill handed Jota his first start since returning from his 18-month lay-off. The Portuguese winger showed some good touches on the left without making a major impact and made way for the fit-again Yang Hyun-jun at half-time.

A Remembrance Day silence lasted barely 20 seconds, with boos coming from all sides of the stadium. The lower tier of the standing section was empty until the Green Brigade and other fans started to file in from the concourse when referee Beaton’s whistle signalled the end of the tribute.

They would have entered to their team one goal behind had Tom Lowery delivered a more emphatic finish after Owen’s cross set him up inside 40 seconds. Sam Johnstone pulled off a double save to deny the midfielder.

Hogh had another good chance soon after his disallowed goal when Duran played him through, but the former Bodo/Glimt forward’s attempt hit the foot of goalkeeper Nico Mantl.

The Dane soon set up Colby Donovan with a clever backheel, but the right-back fired just wide.

Celtic opened the scoring when Scales ran unchallenged to volley Duran’s cross past a static Mantl from 10 yards.

Killie were very much in the game and Johnstone saved from Michael Schjonning-Larsen before Tyreece John-Jules failed to make the most of a good opportunity.

Mantl saved Nygren’s free-kick and he was a busy man after the interval.

The Killie keeper saved from Duran and the Colombian, Donovan, Hogh, Yang and James Forrest all missed the target from half chances.

Baur had a goal disallowed for offside and Hogh was denied by a brilliant diving block from MJ Kamson-Kamara when Kieran Tierney’s cross fell invitingly.

Mantl stopped Nygren’s penalty after Aaron Tshibola was penalised for handball and the goalkeeper soon denied the Swede again from open play.

Baur went off with a knock before Yang escaped a second yellow card, despite appearing to pull down Nicky Clescenco.

Killie soon got their big chance to level, but Owen could not convert.

#2071. Sources: Man United will do 'due diligence' on Mauricio Pochettino move

Transfer Correspondent AUTHORITY Former Sky Sports and ESPN FC correspondent who specialises in global recruitment, contract negotiations, and high-velocity transfer breaking news. FOCUS Exclusive reporting, domestic and international transfer markets, and elite-level insights. THE INSIGHT Pete utilises a Global Network of Industry Sources to deliver verified, first-to-market reporting. His “Deep-Lens” analysis connects the dots between boardroom strategy and pitch-level recruitment, providing a level of transfer clarity that goes beyond surface-level rumours.

Manchester United will explore the option of appointing Mauricio Pochettino if they decide to sack Michael Carrick, sources have told Football Insider.

The Argentine is a long-term target for the Old Trafford hierarchy, and they view him as a clear option once again to potentially replace Carrick.

The 54-year-old penned a new contract with the USA national team in the summer, which is understood to potentially make it a "difficult" appointment for United to line up.

Nevertheless, sources say that the Red Devils will do their "due diligence" on Pochettino in a bid to discover whether they can break that contract.

The Manchester giants are still assessing Carrick's long-term future, but that hasn't stopped them from exploring other options.

The likes of Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann have been heavily linked in recent weeks, and now Pochettino is also in the frame.

Pochettino has been on United's radar for several years now, and he has been linked with the top job at Old Trafford many times before.

However, his move to take charge of the USA national team has served as a major change of direction for his career.

The former Tottenham boss is no stranger to links for a return to the Premier League, and was even tipped to move back to Spurs at times last season.

United are keen to delve deeper into his situation in the USA, but they may find it difficult to prise him away from that role.

His new deal has tied him down until 2030 in theory, which would not make it a cheap deal for United to do.

Football Insider revealed last week that United may find it difficult to sign Manchester City left-back Rayan Ait Nouri unless he "pushes" for a move in January.

Carrick and Co. are desperate to bring in a new left-back, and have turned their attention towards the 25-year-old, who is yet to make a single Premier League appearance this season.

Nevertheless, a deal is understood to be difficult for United at this stage due to the bitter rivalry between the two clubs.

Ait Nouri is expected to have to push for the move to Old Trafford himself in order for City to consider granting it.

#2070. Player Ratings: AC Milan 0-2 Ferencvaros – Torriani howler; several struggle

AC Milan failed to revive their Europa League campaign, losing 2-0 at home to Ferencvaros. Several players failed to perform and below are the ratings for the Rossoneri.

After a mere three points in three games, Milan headed into the clash knowing that a win was more or less a must. Sadly, that didn’t show on the pitch as Ferencvaros deservedly got all of the glory, with the Rossoneri struggling on many fronts.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

If you haven’t already, make sure to check out how we decide the player ratings. From the scale to what affects the rating, we have compiled everything there.

👎 Torriani (4.5): It wasn’t the kindest of backpasses just before the first goal, but man, he needed to do so much better with the first touch. Heavy with all caps would be the way to describe it. In fairness to him, he couldn’t do anything about the first goal and made several good stops throughout.

👔 Amorim (4): In my opinion, this was more of a tactical failure rather than individuals letting Milan down. Ferencvaros had full control of the game and not even bringing on the big guns helped the gaffer. We all warned that the rotation perhaps wasn’t the best idea either.

Torriani (4.5): It wasn’t the kindest of backpasses just before the first goal, but man, he needed to do so much better with the first touch. Heavy with all caps would be the way to describe it. In fairness to him, he couldn’t do anything about the first goal and made several good stops throughout.

Terracciano (5): Was he the difference between a win and a defeat? Absolutely not, but also showed (once again) that he’s just not good enough. Poor defending on several occasions, cheap tricks that many referees would punish, and a general insecurity in possession. The cross attempt in the second half says it all.

De Winter (5.5): That backpass for Torriani should never be played in that way, even if Maignan is between the sticks. He admittedly got a bit unlucky with his clearance in the second half, but even then perhaps he could have done better. Anyway, for me it’s the pass which brings his rating down.

Diawara (5.5): He got beaten a few times at the back, but there weren’t any fatal errors and there were also a couple of good moments. However, overall, I would say it was just below an average display by him.

Bartesaghi (5): He knows how to run on the left flank, that’s for sure, but more often than not he doesn’t really get to the ball even if the pass is good. Also struggled a bit in possession tonight. One sequence was very telling when he tried to shield the ball and lost out completely instead.

Hutchinson (5): Awfully quiet in the first half and when he did get going in the second, there wasn’t much end product to his game. One good save denied him a goal, but he also missed a very good chance and didn’t have any luck with his crosses, really.,

Musah (5): There was one really poor giveaway at the start of the first half, in a proper Musah-esque way, and it probably should have resulted in a goal. Nothing about the rest of his performance was convincing either.

Jashari (5): Just like Musah, he nearly gifted a goal with a huge giveaway in the first half and it wasn’t a surprise to see him come off in the second half. The long balls didn’t have much accuracy and he struggled with Ferencvaros’ pressing.

Cisse (5.5): Milan didn’t really attack much in the first half, so that didn’t help him at all. However, even when he did end up in possession, I don’t think he was that good.

Rabiot (5): Given he wore the captain’s armband tonight and arguably is one of Milan’s best players, this was way below what we can demand from him. No luck in attack, both in terms of passes and finishes, and he also lost the ball a few times when the away side pressed high.

Ramos (5): The €74m man continues to struggle. There were some positive glimpses tonight and you cannot single him out as the worst player on the pitch, but he still needs to do so much more in his role.

Gila (5): He was way too rash just before the second goal, which opened up all the space even if Ferencvaros got a bit lucky. Before that, he had a poor giveaway and also had one right at the end, playing a weak pass to Torriani.

Moreira (6): As expected, the Belgian added energy to the game and also had some success on that right flank, sending several dangerous crosses into the box.

Pulisic (6): Just like Moreira, there was a noticeable difference as Milan were able to keep hold of the ball in the final third for much longer. However, the tactics probably let him and Moreira down in terms of actually being able to do something.

Modric (6): It didn’t take long for him to show that he remains fresh even at that age with a sprint to take control of the ball, and the rest was solid.

Amorim (4): In my opinion, this was more of a tactical failure rather than individuals letting Milan down. Ferencvaros had full control of the game and not even bringing on the big guns helped the gaffer. We all warned that the rotation perhaps wasn’t the best idea either.

#2069. Ronald Araujo agrees with Liverpool’s position on his £47m buy option

Liverpool would prefer to wait until the end of the season before deciding whether or not to activate Ronald Araujo’s £47m buy option.

That’s the claim coming out of SPORT, with the defender himself also understood to prefer delaying a decision until the summer.

According to the outlet in question, the Reds are thought to be “very pleased” with the Uruguayan international. However, the club is very aware of the fact that it will take a somewhat significant figure to bring the centre-back to Anfield on a permanent basis.

But barring a sudden, unexpected collapse of truly cosmic proportions, it’s difficult to see how Liverpool could manage to justify not activating the buy option come the summer.

Even if the club’s long-term plan is to use a less conservative option at right-back, the fact of the matter is they’re going to be quite short on centre-back options come the end of the season.

Club skipper Virgil van Dijk (contracted until 2027) may yet sign an extension, but we can’t see Joe Gomez staying put beyond the summer window. Either way, and even assuming that Giovanni Leoni returns from his ACL injury in excellent shape and has a significant second half of the season at L4, the Reds will need to bolster the department to the tune of potentially two bodies.

Activating Araujo’s buy option, then, feels like a necessity rather than a luxury, especially given the experience that could walk out of the door at the end of the campaign.

SPORT go on to claim that Araujo “is aware that Barcelona is keeping a close eye on him”, which doesn’t really communicate a great deal as far as intention is concerned.

Prior reporting has indicated that Barca boss Hansi Flick will hold some sway in the player’s next move this summer, but ultimately, it should be emphasised that Liverpool Football Club handed the footballer a new lease of life. Not Barcelona. And we’d like to think that’ll count for something in the long run.

#2068. Scott Parker already 'at risk' at West Ham as 'big problems' emerge

West Ham United could find themselves in a difficult position over Scott Parker if their results do not improve quickly.

Parker took charge of his first game as the new manager at the weekend, but saw his side fall to a 2-1 defeat against Blackburn at Ewood Park, leading to concerns.

While West Ham are convinced their new manager is the right man to lead them forward, and the Blackburn defeat is not on him, they are expecting a rapid turnaround.

Former West Ham scout Mick Brown told Football Insider that the board have placed themselves in a difficult position following their decision to sack Nuno Espirito Santo.

The Hammers have now made it clear that they expect to get promoted this season, and anything less will be deemed a failure, ramping up the pressure at the London Stadium.

Parker must ensure he meets those expectations, or he will also face pressure from the board and the supporters, who expressed their frustrations at Ewood Park.

Football Insider revealed on 6 November that West Ham are convinced that Parker is the right man to lead them back into the Premier Leaugue come the end of the season.

The 46-year-old has previously led Fulham, Bournemouth and Burnley to promotion, and there is optimism that he will do the same with the Hammers come next summer.

However, there are concerns that the conditions at West Ham may not be ideal for the new manager, who is likely to come under pressure if their struggles continue.

"I did think it was a strange decision to go for Scott Parker, but I have heard good things around him," Brown told Football Insider.

"He's got a good record in the Championship, so that's a positive, but there are bigger problems at West Ham than who the manager is.

"I felt this way during my time there, and certainly after I left, but I have no faith in the West Ham board to make the right decisions and set the team up to be successful.

"Regardless of whether it was the right decision to sack Nuno and appoint Parker, that's not going to change the makeup of this squad.

"On paper, they should be more than good enough to win promotion to the Premier League, but recent results have proved it's not always as easy as maybe it should be.

"The problem now for Parker is, he has to turn their results around and get a positive feeling back, because otherwise he will come under pressure as well.

"West Ham have set a precedent, if they don't feel results have been good enough, they will make changes. So if Parker isn't getting results, will he be at risk as well? I wouldn't rule it out."

West Ham have been clear about what they expect for the coming season, with pressure on to earn promotion back to the Premier League at the first time of asking.

Failure to do so would be calamitous for the London Stadium club, and their decision to part ways with Nuno was based on fears they may not be able to achieve that goal.

Brown warned Football Insider prior to Nuno's dismissal that West Ham have made their demands clear and will not accept anything less than positive results.

Ultimately, defeats at home to Southampton and West Brom sparked major concerns amongst the board, and they decided to pull the trigger on the manager.

That could now be the same for Parker, and if he proves unable to turn West Ham's form around and lead them back to the top, questions will also be asked of him.

#2066. 'I've looked at it a few times' - Ex-refs chief shares verdict after analysing Patrick Dorgu footage vs Aston Villa

Patrick Dorgu's equaliser against Aston Villa was rightfully awarded to Manchester United.

That is the opinion of former head of PGMOL and FIFA referee Keith Hackett, speaking exclusively to Football Insider.

Aston Villa and the Red Devils played out an enthralling eight-goal thriller that was not short of contentious decisions.

Two penalties were awarded on the night, and complaints were made by the Villa's defence after conceding in the closing minutes.

Zion Suzuki led those efforts to get the goal checked over by VAR, but in the end, it was allowed to stand.

With Hackett delivering his thoughts on the decision.

Goalkeepers are extremely protected between the sticks, and often any infringement on them is put forward as a possible foul.

When Suzuki looked to claim the ball from United's last-gasp corner, Senne Lammens positioned himself right in front of his opposing counterpart.

The Belgian did enough to both put off the Japanese shot-stopper, while also avoiding a foul, at least according to Hackett.

Hackett said: "I think when you look at it, and I looked at it a couple of times last night, I think the goalkeeper's [Lammens] actions really have taken place after the goalkeeper [Suzuki] has missed going for the ball.

"And, you know, when a goalkeeper comes out, he's got a fair amount of protection, but he's got to effectively win the ball and win it cleanly. And I think this is poor goalkeeping rather than actually a foul that should be awarded."

"So I'm saying that I'm allowing the goal. I'm happy with the goal because I think that action by the opposing player was after the event, not during the course of it."

Hackett was also left impressed with how Kavanagh generally officiated the 4-4 draw seeing as there were a number of incidents.

He said: "So, look, I thought Kavanagh officiated quite well yesterday. I thought it was one of his better performances.

"I think the game has to recognise that we have two UEFA elite referees. We might have an opinion about those two, Michael Oliver and Chris Kavanagh, but they've satisfied UEFA that they are elite officials.

"And therefore, as such, a game of this nature needed a top-class referee on it."

Villa fans may not agree, and there will be plenty of United fans who were left unhappy as well.

But two sets of unhappy fans with the referee is often a sign he was fair in his judgements.

#2065. Iraola admits uncertainty over Liverpool player’s international involvement after injury scare

Andoni Iraola has expressed concern as to whether one Liverpool player will link up with his country during this month’s international break.

The Reds go into the brief pause to the season off the back of a 3-1 victory at Crystal Palace, with some of the gloss from that result removed by a questionable stoppage-time penalty for the home side and an injury scare to Dominik Szoboszlai.

The 26-year-old pulled up towards the end of the first half at Selhurst Park on Sunday and played with a knee brace after the interval until he was substituted for Trey Nyoni in the 69th minute.

After the match, Iraola admitted that the Hungarian wasn’t operating at 100% yesterday, having only recently returned from a thigh issue.

The Basque said (via liverpoolfc.com): “I don’t know [if it’s] a problem, but he definitely wasn’t 100%. Let’s see. The last thing we need now is to lose players in the international games.

“Last time, in the international break, we lost three very important players, so now I’m praying – it’s the last thing we need.

“I think he extended a little bit the knee. It was fine, but not 100%, so he has to be careful to see if he can play with the national team or not. We will see, and also hope that it doesn’t happen like the other break where we lost Alex [Isak], Cody [Gakpo] and Dom. Touch wood we are in a better place in two weeks.”

On whether Szoboszlai would link up with the Hungary squad for their upcoming UEFA Nations League fixtures, Iraola said: “I know he will do everything to go because he loves to play with the national team, but he was not 100% when he finished the game. I suppose they will have to analyse, the medical staff, and see what it is.

“I know what I want, but I also have to understand the national teams. I’m sure that Dom, if he is fine he will want to go, but I’m not sure if he’s going to be fine.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Along with Iraola, Liverpool fans with no vested interest in the Hungary national team will surely be hoping that Szoboszlai rests up during the international window rather than representing his country.

Marco Rossi’s side are away to Georgia next Saturday and at home to Northern Ireland three days later, with promotion to League A well within their grasp heading into that double header.

As captain of his country, the midfielder will no doubt be striving to play his part over the coming week or so, but there must also be a duty towards the club which pays his wages and given him a platform to reach an even higher level in his career.

Liverpool resume their season in 13 days’ time with an Anfield grudge match against Manchester United, and they still have 11 more matches to play before the end of December, so managing players’ fitness will be vital during that relentless period.

Szoboszlai has been a frustrating figure at times this term, with debate raging as to where exactly his best position is on the pitch, but his creativity came to the fore in the win over Palace on Sunday.

Also, as he’s shown on several occasions, he possesses that X-factor to conjure up show-stopping and often result-altering goals.

Whatever decisions might be taken between Liverpool and Hungary, fingers crossed that our vice-captain is back to 100% for the Man United clash on the 22nd of this month.

#2064. Hearts ‘embarrassment’ as furious Vrancken lets rip after Falkirk nightmare

Wouter Vrancken condemned a “ridiculous” first-half display from his sorry Hearts side as their 18-month unbeaten home record in the William Hill Premiership was ripped apart by ruthless Falkirk.

The beleaguered Jambos, who went into the game without 11 players through injury following a gruelling run of fixtures, endured a dismal afternoon as the Bairns raced into a 4-0 half-time lead on their way to a 5-2 victory at Tynecastle.

Finley Barbrook, Owen Eames, Liam Henderson and Jacob Murrell’s double had the visitors 5-0 up within 47 minutes before Hearts reduced the deficit through substitute Sabri Guendouz and a Claudio Braga penalty.

It was a first league defeat at Tynecastle since April 2025 for the Jambos, who have now won just two of their last 11 matches in all competitions.

Read more: Liam Scales strike enough to drag Celtic across line in Kilmarnock win

“This is an embarrassment, the first half for sure,” said Vrancken. “Always doubting, always doing things half-half, in possession, out of possession, everything, and such easy goals again.

“When you give those easy goals, then you cannot win a game. It’s childish goals and cannot happen on this level. Those simple things, they are the basics actually in these situations.

“It’s crazy, crazy, and everybody – me, staff, players – have to take responsibility in those things. This is ridiculous.”

To exacerbate their grim predicament, the Jambos lost yet another senior player as defender Malachi Fagan-Walcott limped off in the second half.

“This also makes me a bit angry, because now we lose Mal again,” said Vrancken.

“Hopefully it’s not too bad, but still we had to replace him there, because he was one of the guys who were good in the game and in the last games actually he had a really consistent, good level.”

Hearts were leapfrogged into third place by Falkirk, who made it five top-flight wins in a row for the first time in 31 years.

“I’ve never been 5-0 up here before,” said Bairns manager John McGlynn. “First half we were outstanding. A great start to the game for us to get the goal so early.

“It was well documented about the Hearts injuries and, coming off the back of the game on Thursday night (in Thun), it was always going to be difficult for them.

“We had to smell blood and we had to go for it and that’s exactly what happened. The goals and our play were outstanding in the first half. We won every duel, we won everything all over the park.

“We got ourselves 4-0 up at half-time, which is dreamland. At 3pm, we never expected to be 4-0 up at half-time and certainly not 5-0 up a few minutes into the second half, which was another really good goal in transition.

“Hearts had a lot at the ball and dominated the second period, but we’re taking 5-2 every day of the week, make no mistake about it. It jumps us up into third place.

“Winning five on the trot has not been done since 1995, Jim Jefferies’ team, so I’m delighted for everyone at the football club that we’ve managed to equal that record.”

#2062. Noni Madueke may be the key to reviving Bukayo Saka, Mikel Arteta has a secret Arsenal tactic

Correspondent AUTHORITY NCTJ-qualified football journalist with experience at VAVEL, Hayters TV, SPORTbible, and Centredevils. FOCUS Premier League analysis, tactical deep-dives, and original opinion content across Arsenal, Chelsea, Tottenham, Manchester City, and Celtic. THE INSIGHT Evan utilises a network of club and industry contacts to deliver verified, high-speed reporting. He provides specialist tactical and analytical content to ensure fans get beyond the headlines and understand the full picture.

Bukayo Saka will be itching to return to action for Arsenal as he watches Noni Madueke thrive in his position.

The 25-year-old has been missing since October's trip to Bayern Munich, where he suffered an injury to his quad.

In his 11 appearances before the injury, the England international had scored four goals and provided an assist, but was still some way off the levels he can reach.

Madueke replaced him in the starting line-up and has been superb on the right of the attack, putting in another superb display as Arsenal beat Hull City 1-0 on Saturday.

The 24-year-old, who joined the Gunners in a £52million deal in the summer of 2025, has not always been convincing, but finally looks to be showing why Mikel Arteta targeted him.

Should his form continue, Saka may even face a serious battle for his position when he does return from injury.

Noni Madueke has been in fine form for Arsenal and leads the way in the Premier League for chances created per match 👏📊 pic.twitter.com/p3hxg9FWHR

Madueke's strong form has come at exactly the right time for Arteta, who can use it to light a fire under Saka.

The winger has struggled with injuries over the last two years, but he remains a hugely capable player and has not been able to show it.

Yet with him now having been forced to sit at home and watch as Madueke takes the Arsenal acclaim from his position, there should now be new motivation for Saka to get back to his best.

His position for England is in threat, too, if he does not. Thomas Tuchel opted against selecting Madueke for November's camp, but he will undoubtedly be involved should his strong form continue.

Saka had been set to miss around eight weeks of action with the quad injury, but will hope to return ahead of schedule.

Arteta will be well aware of the effect Madueke's form may have on Saka because he is encouraging the same competition throughout the squad.

William Saliba's return will see him compete for Ezri Konsa's place, Piero Hincapie is targeting Riccardo Calafiori's spot and there are several other examples in the Arsenal squad.

"We have really good options because they're in the right mindset," Arteta said last month. "I'm extremely proud of the chemistry and the desire we have created among the players who both start and finish the game.

"We've seen a great example with Ebz [Eberechi Eze], who could have been upset and certainly was when he was substituted after 45 minutes at Forest, and then came in and made the impact he did on Wednesday.

"That's exactly what you need - you have a bench that can be strong as strong as you want, but they have to give you what you need."

#2060. “It’s about ambition, concentration, desire” – Amorim tears into Milan after Ferencvaros defeat

AC Milan head coach Ruben Amorim did not hold back on his team’s performance after the 2-0 Europa League defeat to Ferencvaros.

Milan needed a win having lost two of their first three games in Europe, and instead they responded with perhaps their worst performance under Amorim. Lenny Joseph’s second-half brace was enough for Ferencvaros to emerge with three points that their performance merited in truth.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The decision was made to rotate again with six changes from the win over Inter, but in the second half the likes of Christian Pulisic, Diego Moreira, Mario Gila and Luka Modric all came on. The end result was the same: frustration and an inability to piece together the required quality.

Amorim spoke to Sky after Koni De Winter offered his opinion that it is a psychological issue for the team. The words from the manager were transcribed by MilanNews.

You issued a warning that today would be complication…

“There’s no explanation. There’s nothing I can say, especially about the first half. I don’t remember another first half like it. It’s about ambition, concentration, desire. We gave away opportunities, we gave away stupid gifts. We weren’t prepared to play football tonight.”

“It’s hard to explain. We simply weren’t ready to move from the derby to this other competition. When you play for Milan, you have a responsibility, and you can’t show up like that. I probably didn’t ensure the team took to the field ready either.”

De Winter says it’s a matter of mentality…

“We’re not ready to be competitive on two fronts. We need to work on our way of looking at football and how we approach matches. There are no excuses tonight, there’s nothing I can say.

“I usually have a lot to say in defence of our team, but not tonight. We need to be more humble and understand what happened.”

“Maybe I did something wrong these past two days, but not mentally. This team had similar problems last year. We have to find a solution. Tonight we weren’t ready, we weren’t brave. If we don’t win, we’ll have to do everything we can to turn things around, and we didn’t see that.

“Everyone needs to train like Pavlovic. He’s ready to die in training. He’s a good example. Sometimes when players don’t start, they struggle. But there are no excuses; we should have won even with those who started.”

“We have to fix this! We can’t just assume it’s going to be like this. We should have done so many things better tonight. Just being better on second balls would have been much better. We weren’t in the game tonight.”

How important is the Europa League now? It’s a complicated situation…

“I have to focus on the league, obviously, but we also have to do well in the Europa League. We must and can win games despite the rotation. We have to be ready – we’re not now – to play and win every three days.

“But I won’t give up on this competition. But as long as the mathematics don’t condemn us, we’ll fight in this competition as we do in the others.”

#2058. Haissem Hassan Celtic absence explained as ‘manoeuvring’ costs winger

Martin O'Neill has explained Haissem Hassan's omission from Celtic's matchday squad against Kilmarnock on Sunday afternoon.

The Egyptian winger has been in and out of the Hoops' starting XI in recent weeks and performed well despite still only producing two assists from his 17 total appearances.

Hassan, 24, has had to bide his time for a proper lengthy run in the team but he was not involved at all as Celtic narrowly pipped Killie in a 1-0 victory at Parkhead.

His omission from the team sheet before kick-off had fans curious as to whether or not the playmaker had perhaps sustained an injury at Lennoxtown in the build-up.

However manager O'Neill instead revealed it was "manoeuvring" that has kept the attacker out of the squad with Camilo Duran picked on the flank instead and Kasper Hogh through the middle.

Yang and James Forrest were the two wide men who were on the bench for the Hoops and O'Neill made his thoughts public.

"How is (Hassan)? We're trying to do, as much as possible, we're trying to do a bit of manoeuvring at this minute. I just think it'll be great for places.

"If there's proper competition for places, it can only make us better."

#2057. Alexis Mac Allister shares what one Crystal Palace player told him about Alisson on Sunday

Alisson Becker’s outstanding performance in Liverpool’s 3-1 win away to Crystal Palace on Sunday was reflected in what one Eagles player told Alexis Mac Allister.

The Reds’ number 1 had shipped criticism in recent days for errors in the defeats to Arsenal and Fenerbahce, but he was back to his world-class best at Selhurst Park yesterday as he turned in a man-of-the-match display for his side.

The Brazilian pulled off six saves in total against Pierre Sage’s team, including a stunning reaction stop to keep out a fearsome volley from Daichi Kamada just a couple of minutes before the Argentine scored the visitors’ opening goal.

Speaking to BBC Sport after the match (via liverpoolfc.com), Mac Allister was singing Alisson’s praises and shared what the Japan international had told him about the Liverpool goalkeeper.

The Reds’ number 10 said of the Brazil stopper: “He’s so good, especially the save from Kamada’s shot [in the first half]. Kamada couldn’t believe the save he made and he was telling me, but that’s who he is.

“He is an amazing goalkeeper and an amazing guy as well. I’m really, really happy for him.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Alisson had endured some unusually shaky moments in recent weeks, but he reminded us all on Sunday that class is permanent and that he remains pivotal to Liverpool’s hopes of success this season.

In addition to the outstanding save from Kamada, he also produced excellent stops to keep out an Adam Wharton header just before half-time and a double save from Yeremy Pino and Jefferson Lerma in the 77th minute when the Reds were 2-0 to the good.

That Palace scored just once from an xG of 2.6 yesterday sums up just how imperious our number 1 had been, and it’s no wonder that the Eagles’ Japanese attacker was stunned by the 34-year-old’s brilliance.

Such was Alisson’s performance at Selhurst Park that the Premier League’s official X profile posted a compilation of his saves from the win over the south London outfit, with the goalkeeper treating us to his own showreel.

Anyone who might’ve thought that the Brazil international was in irreversible decline was made to think again yesterday by a masterclass from Liverpool’s legendary number 1.

#2054. 'Hammer foot, It's a belter' - Brighton player ratings vs Brentford as 9/10 midfield ace does it again

Brighton moved to second in the Premier League with a comfortable 2-0 win against Brentford at the Amex Stadium.

Brighton's opening goal on 15 minutes was a thing of beauty as Diego Gomez fired in an absolute rocket with his left foot from 25 yards. It adds to the Paraguayan's collection of spectacular goals for Brighton - including his halfway line effort against Crystal Palace in his previous appearance at the Amex.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Brighton's task was made easier as the Bees were reduced to 10-men when Igor Thiago was dismissed on 23 minutes for shoving his arm in the face of Brighton midfielder Chema Andres.

The second soon arrived 20 minutes later as Keane Lewis-Potter tangled with Luka Vuskovic in the area as they jostled at a set-piece and referee Michael Oliver awarded a penalty. Pascal Gross confidently smashed it into the top corner.

Brighton dominated for most of the second half as 10-man Brentford sat deep but failed to add to their tally. Fabian Hurzeler’s high-flying Seagulls resume Premier League action after the international break on November 22 at Hull City.

Bart Verbruggen - 7: The Dutchman kept Brighton’s seventh clean sheet of the season - the highest in the division. One of the easiest matches of his Premier League career as the Bees failed to register a shot on target.

Costinha - 7: The Protugese right back has ben an excellent addition following his summer arrival. More than proved his worth in Ferdi Kadioglu’s absence.

Luka Vuskovic - 8: Rarely seen a 6ft 4in centre back with a better first touch than Luka Vuskovic. The 19-year-old continues to impress after his £50m summer arrival. Enjoyed a physical tussle.

Lewis Dunk - 6: His job was made so much easier after Thiago's red card. A pretty easy afternoon for the skipper who can now put his feet up during the international break. Picked up a needless booking on 61 minutes.

Olivier Boscagli - 8: Fine delivery from the left to set up De Cuyper's early chance. Defended well and provided width on the left. He’s started every single match so far this term in all competitions. Very good!

Chema Andres - 7: A real smooth operator in the midfield. Offers more composure and balance than Carlos Baleba ever did. Booked midway through the half and replaced at halftime for Mats Wieffer.

Pascal Gross - 7: Another who has started every match this season and will have a deserved break during the internationals. Smashed home his penalty on style and faultless in midfield.

Diego Gomez - 9: Lewis Dunk calls him "hammer foot". What a belter! The Paraguayan was full throttle all match.

Yasin Ayari - 7: Forced a decent save from Brentford keeper Kelleher on 44 minutes. The Sweden international plays at a consistently high level these days. replaced by Hinshelwood on 78 minutes.

Maxim De Cuyper - 7: Headed an early chance over the bar and the Belgian would have been disappointed not to add to his four goals and four assists this term. Replaced by Minteh for the final 10.

Charalampos Kostoulas - 6: The Greek striker had a couple of chances - one header from distance and one clever lobbed attempt - but very little fell his way. Impressive work rate. Taken of in the closing stages for Georginio.

Substitutions: Wieffer (Chema, h-t), Hinshelwood (Ayari, 78) Georginio (Kostoulas, 82) Minteh (De Cuyper, 82), Yalcouye (Gomez, 92)

#2050. Pitcher perfect: Charlie’s strike hands Steyning Town victory over Horley

Town were without several key men so made a few adjustments to the team – but still lined up looking strong, showing the increasing competition for places.

The first half was one that certainly saw Steyning in the ascendancy; however they were unable to turn possession to decent opportunities as both keepers remained largely untested.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The game sprang into life minutes before half-time as the busy Leo Ginger cut in from the left and let rip a stunning dipping strike from 25 yards that flew into the top right hand corner off the post.

What a great way to go into half-time… or so we thought. The visitors had other ideas as they hit back almost immediately breaking well at the other end of the pitch culminating in a fine finish into the top of the net by Abdulahi Abdulazeez.

The second period followed much of the pattern of the first, with the Barrowmen having the bulk of possession and playing some good football but lacking a bit of cutting edge.

The defining moment of the match came with 18 minutes to go as Charlie Pitcher broke down the right, taking a floating through ball superbly in his stride with a couple of great touches before sweeping home the winner in style. A great goal to win a less-than-great game.

Town saw out the remainder of the game with minimal fuss as they added three vital points to their league tally. The day was pretty much about grinding at a result when not at your best and overall it was really positive to do that when other games have got away from the team late on this season.

Steyning are 15th and next up – on Saturday – is a big test away to high-flying Hastings United.

#2048. Liverpool told they have a ‘high energy’ dynamo who gives them ‘a chance’ of being in a title race

One player could give Liverpool ‘a chance’ of being involved in the Premier League title race this season if he stays ‘fit and available’.

That’s according to Troy Deeney, who made such claims about Alexis Mac Allister after another standout performance from the midfielder in the Reds’ 3-1 victory over Crystal Palace on Sunday.

The Argentine opened the scoring with a close-range header shortly before half-time, taking his goal tally for the season to five and matching his haul from the entirety of 2025/26.

Despite the 27-year-old’s consistently top-class displays, he’s yet to be offered a new contract by Liverpool, a situation which has baffled Deeney.

The former Watford striker selected Mac Allister in his Premier League team of the week for BBC Sport, outlining: ‘How this guy has not got a new deal I don’t know. He keeps coming up big, high energy, and he is vitally important to the way Liverpool play.

‘When he is fit and available and firing on all cylinders, it feels like they have a chance in this title race.’

(Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

The World Cup winner was one of the Reds’ biggest disappointments in a chastening 2025/26 season for the club, but he’s been among the standout performers for his team since Andoni Iraola took the reins from Arne Slot over the summer.

Not only is Mac Allister chipping in with a steady supply of goals, he also showed his commitment to the cause and to his teammates by confronting Jefferson Lerma in the closing stages when the Palace player got involved in a spat with young Trey Nyoni.

With a gap of nine points to make up on leaders Arsenal, it’ll take a remarkable level of consistency from Liverpool to haul themselves into genuine title contention going into the latter weeks of the campaign.

Could our number 10 potentially elevate us into the title picture if he maintains this standard of performance? In truth it’ll require the rest of his teammates to follow suit, rather than being overly depending on just one or two individuals.

For now, though, Mac Allister just needs to keep up what he’s been doing since August and mind the disciplinary tightrope – he’s one yellow card away from a suspension in the Premier League, and two in the Champions League.

On current form, Liverpool can’t afford to be without the Argentine for long.

#2046. 3-man panel split over Celtic VAR flashpoint as key ref claim made

Frustrated Kasper Hogh thought his long wait for a Celtic goal was finally over against Kilmarnock.

The Dane was desperate to end a barren run stretching back 15 games when he fired beyond Nico Mantl during the first half of the Hoops’ narrow 1-0 victory.

And the celebrations erupted when Hogh finished from seven yards after being picked out by Benjamin Nygren, seemingly bringing his lengthy goal drought to an end.

But his joy was short-lived. VAR spotted a potential foul by Mika Baur on Kilmarnock skipper Greg Kiltie earlier in the build-up and referee John Beaton was summoned to the pitchside monitor.

Read more: Watch Ex-SPFL boss see red after astonishing rammy with former Premiership star

Beaton needed only a quick look before deciding Baur had fouled Kiltie and chalking off the strike. Hogh’s barren run ultimately stretched to 16 games, although Liam Scales struck in the 26th minute to secure all three points for Celtic.

But was it the right call? The major flashpoint certainly split opinion among those watching on, with one branding the decision “soft” and another adamant the officials had got it spot on. Here’s what three onlookers had to say about the big VAR call.

Speaking on Celtic TV, Donnelly said: “At the time, I thought he had won the ball, but he might get a touch on the Kilmarnock player’s foot. I thought he had won the ball back brilliantly. It’s soft. It’s a fantastic team goal. I thought Baur had done brilliantly.”

Speaking on BBC Sportsound, McFadden said: “I mean, it looked like he didn’t even get to the monitor. Maybe he didn’t have to.

“Watching it live, it looked like a clean challenge and good play by Mika Baur, but it must have been pretty clear.”

Grant, however, backed the officials. Speaking on Celtic TV, he said: “Everything was excellent about it. All the players were involved, Hogh was delighted, then it’s here.

“It’s a free-kick. He has not got the ball. I have got to be honest, if you don’t get the ball, then it’s a free-kick, and it is a free-kick. We would be complaining if it was anyone else, but Baur does it that well I didn’t notice it at the time. It’s only when you see it on the replay.”

#2044. Michael Carrick answers Man Utd quit question as crisis hits alarming new low

Michael Carrick insisted he would not walk away from Manchester United after Sunday’s wild 4-4 draw with Aston Villa ensured his side would spend the international window languishing in the relegation zone.

Stoppage-time goals from Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu saw United rally for an unlikely point on a day when they started both halves by allowing Villa to storm into two-goal leads before coming back.

The point means United sit 18th in the table, doing little to ease the intense scrutiny on Carrick given they are now eight league games without a win – a club record in the Premier League era – with their only victory of the season back in August against newly-promoted Ipswich.

Read more: Haissem Hassan Celtic absence explained as ‘manoeuvring’ costs winger

Asked on Sky Sports if he would quit if he felt it was the right thing to do for the club, Carrick said: “That’s not going to happen.”

Then, speaking in his post-match press conference, Carrick expressed confidence his side could still turn things around this season.

“One hundred per cent,” he said. “I think there’s more than enough. Goals change games and we’ve got to deal with it and it’s something we have to improve on drastically. But there’s more than enough, we’re just making it too difficult for ourselves at the moment in certain times…

“I’m quite clear with what direction the club needs to go in. We’ve just got to win games.”

United were 2-0 down inside five minutes as Alysson and Nicolas Jackson pounced on defensive errors, but Bruno Fernandes got one back from the penalty spot before Youri Tielemans scored against his former club.

Having worked so hard to get level, United conceded twice in the opening seven minutes of the second half to John McGinn’s penalty and Leon Goretzka’s first Villa goal, with many fans having left before their second comeback of the afternoon.

“Football is about moments, football is about what happens in both boxes in the end,” Carrick added.

“Take (away) the moments and the totally avoidable goals we’ve given away, I actually thought we played pretty well, we were the better team for the most part and I’m disappointed we haven’t won the game.”

Unai Emery, among the candidates touted as a potential successor to Carrick, was visibly frustrated at conceding the late equaliser.

“The referee added six minutes, I think the match was done…” Emery said. “I am angry of course. How to accept to lose in the last six minutes with two goals is difficult…

“I’m angry not with the players, angry with the situation. You are winning in the last six minutes, winning in extra time, and we lost the opportunity to have two points more.”

Dorgu headed in from a corner in a crowded penalty box and Emery admitted goalkeeper Zion Suzuki, hugely impressive since joining this summer, still has work to do.

“It is a process, it’s a good example when you concede, it’s (about) adaptation to the Premier League for Zion,” he added.

“They are pushing, they are disturbing the goalkeeper. In some countries, in other leagues, they are not permitting it.

“Here yes, and we have to continue analysing, having experiences and trying to avoid these situations.”

#2037. Rockettes put 10 past Portchester – the match in pictures

The result leaves them second in the table with four wins and a draw from their opening five matches.

Bec Bell-Thorns set up two attacks early on with her runs and crosses from the right. First Kate Delilis diverted a chance over the bar and then a similar move soon after saw Millie Carter shoot high and wide just 3 minutes in. Aimee Hall-Guy did well in the Bognor area following a cross from the right but diverted wide from close range.

Bognor took the lead on 12 minutes when a corner fell to Sophia Poling who nodded it in despite a defender's efforts on the line. The Rockettes extended their lead on 15 minutes as Kate Delillis fired it in off a defender following Lucie Wright's freekick cross. Sophie Humphrey also hit the left post after a short run as Bognor dominated the opening 20 minutes.

Nicole Robinson saved comfortably from Hall-Guy's strike from outside the area. Lily West put a neat through ball to Char Heanen but her powerful strike was pushed over confidently by Robinson on 26 minutes. Lucie Selvester did well to cross the ball into the area to find Sophie Humphrey but after twisting and turning she brought out a good save by Sofie Harris.

Elena Butcher clipped the crossbar with her cross moments later for the visitors. On 33 minutes Poling hit a long range freekick directly high and wide as Bognor maintained their lead. Bognor went three goals up in the 35th minute. The visitors failed to clear their lines from Wright's corner before the ball fell to Humphrey who blasted it high into the roof of the net.

Bognor got their fourth goal on 40 minutes. A fine pass out wide onto the left found Lucie Wright in space and shen ran onto it before firing it over the goalkeeper and into the net. It got better for the hosts as Humphrey netted her second of the afternoon, following up the rebound from a previous strike on 44 minutes. HT 5-0.

After half time Niamh Andersson replaced Bell-Thorns.

Humphrey turned in the area quickly and forced a save over the bar from Harris. Humphrey studded in from close range for Bognor's 6th goal of the afternoon. It was scrappy in defence for the visitors who failed to clear the danger on 48 minutes. On 56 minutes Alice Gue was replaced by Ellie Jefkins.

Bognor made it seven on 58 minutes when Humphrey netted her fourth of the day following a low cross. Delillis set up Freya Boxer but after a nice run she hit the side netting with her strike. Bognor made another change on 62 minutes as Wright came off for Clara Castanheira.

Elena Williams hit a free-kick directly into Robinson's arms in a rare chance for the visitors. Carter's corner kick on the right bounced back out for a goal kick off the frame of goal moments later. Bognor got their 8th in the 66th minute as Humphrey closed down the ball before passing it square to Boxer in the box and she made no mistake, netting it along the deck and in.

Bognor got their ninth on 69 minutes. Andersson placed it nicely beyond defence for Delillis who fired it past the goalkeeper. On 70 minutes Talliah Anderson replaced Sophie Humphrey. Good work from Carter saw her pass back to Castanheira who curled it into the middle where Andersson was waiting but she diverted it wide of goal.

A cross from the left by Castanheira found Boxer in the box and she fired it high and in for Bognor's tenth goal on 76 minutes. A high corner bounced off Elena Williams and into the net for the visitors first goal of the afternoon as a consolation. The visitors also hit the post moments later as the goal perked up the opposition in for the first time in the second half.

Gue came back on for Macie Downs on 86 minutes in a rolling substitution. But despite more chances for Boxer for the Rockettes towards the end it was a comprehensive victory for the Bognor women's side.

They travel to Andover New Street on Sunday, November 15, at 2pm before playing at home on Sunday 22 against AFC Varsity with kick off at 2pm.

#2035. 'Provoked' - Brentford's Keith Andrews makes Chema Andres claim after Igor Thiago red card at Brighton

Brentford boss Keith Andrews questioned the use of VAR in the Premier League after Igor Thiago’s first-half dismissal proved costly in a 2-0 defeat at high-flying Brighton.

Bees striker Thiago was initially shown a yellow card by referee Michael Oliver after reacting to a shirt pull and subsequent push from Albion midfielder Chema Andres, who was also booked.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

But the punishment was upgraded to red on review as match official Oliver deemed the Brazil international used “force” to push his opponent in the face with a raised arm.

Brentford’s only other league defeat this term came after Yehor Yarmoliuk was shown a first-half red card in last month’s 2-1 home loss to Liverpool.

Andrews accepted his players must take responsibility for their conduct but questioned the circumstances surrounding both incidents.

“We’ve lost two games in the league this season and both have been when we’ve gone down to 10 men, so you need to analyse yourself first clearly,” he said.

“On both scenarios, we can do better. On both scenarios, the opposition player has been the one to provoke the situation and antagonise our player and react towards our player in an aggressive way.

“Players’ reactions now mean everything. I’m going to reiterate it: we should do better. But the game is in a state now of a place I don’t particularly like. We’ll have to have a look at that because it’s costing us.”

Brentford were already trailing at the time of Thiago’s sending-off following a stunning long-range opener from Brighton midfielder Diego Gomez.

Disgruntled away fans chanted “2-0 to the referee” and “Michael Oliver, it’s all about you” after Pascal Gross doubled Albion’s lead with a 42nd-minute penalty awarded for Keane Lewis-Potter’s shirt pull on Luka Vuskovic.

Andrews, who felt his side should have been “cuter” in the penalty incident, was frustrated Oliver was sent to the pitch-side monitor before changing his initial decision on Thiago.

“I’m struggling to believe in this day and age where we see the referee’s call on pitch and the bar of where they’re given the licence to referee in-game, which is what I should think it should be, but he’s been sent to the screen,” he said.

“We play on the edge, we’re a team that likes to play on the edge, I want us to be on the edge. But it clearly cost us.”

Brighton climbed to second after marking their return to the Amex Stadium following five successive away matches with a comfortable victory.

Gomez lashed into the top-left corner with his left foot to follow up his goal from the halfway line in last month’s 5-0 thrashing of rivals Crystal Palace.

Seagulls head coach Fabian Hurzeler said: “It’s a funny story because yesterday he trained shooting with the left foot and I couldn’t see him scoring today with this left foot – the shots weren’t great.

“I asked him after the game where he got this quality from overnight. It’s a huge improvement in a very short period.”

Albion’s win was a seventh from 10 top-flight games and lifted them above Manchester City and back to within five points of leaders Arsenal.

Asked when Seagulls supporters can start getting really excited, Hurzeler said: “They should be always excited if they watch our game, and that’s our job to make them excited.

“I always say they can dream, they can have high expectations on us, but these are things we can’t control.”
